questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: My mother-in-law has twelve grandchildren.
questions.explanation: Mi suegra (my mother-in-law) is like ella, so the verb is tiene. Nietos, the masculine plural, covers grandchildren of both sexes.

questions.stem: Complete: "Nosotros ___ en la oficina."
questions.explanation: Location takes estar, and the nosotros form is estamos: Estamos en la oficina (We're at the office). "somos" is ser, which isn't used for where people are; "están" is the ellos/ustedes form and "estoy" the yo form.

questions.stem: Complete: "Mi hermana ___ doctora y hoy ___ en el hospital."
questions.explanation: A job takes ser (es doctora), and where a person is takes estar (está en el hospital). The tempting "está doctora" treats the job like a state, and "es en el hospital" uses ser for a person's location.

questions.stem: It's Sunday and the shop doesn't open. Which sentence says so?
questions.explanation: Whether a shop is open or closed is its condition right now, so Spanish uses estar, and the adjective agrees with la tienda (feminine): La tienda está cerrada. "es cerrada" uses the wrong verb, and "cerrado" doesn't agree with tienda.

questions.stem: After a two-hour meeting, Pablo wants to say "I'm bored." What should he say?
questions.explanation: "Bored" is how he feels now, so estar: Estoy aburrido (masculine, because Pablo is a man). "Soy aburrido" means "I'm a boring person". "aburrida" would be a woman speaking.

questions.stem: Complete: "La fiesta de cumpleaños ___ en mi casa el sábado."
questions.explanation: An event (a party, a class, a concert) takes ser when you say where it takes place: La fiesta es en mi casa. Compare people and things, which take estar: Mis amigos están en mi casa. "son" is plural and "estoy" is yo.

questions.stem: Read Diego's message: "Hola, Ana. Estoy en el centro con mi hermano. Él está muy contento porque la tienda de videojuegos está abierta, pero yo estoy un poco cansado." How does Diego feel?
questions.explanation: Diego says yo estoy un poco cansado: I'm a bit tired. It's his brother (Él) who is muy contento, very happy. Nothing says anyone is worried (preocupado) or sick (enfermo).

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake?
questions.explanation: Where a thing is takes estar: El baño está aquí. Guadalajara está en México is right even though a city never moves: location is always estar. Origin (Somos de Colombia) takes ser, and a state (ocupados) takes estar.

questions.stem: How does each person feel? Choose the adjective for each numbered face.

image.alt: Five cartoon faces in a row, numbered 1 to 5: half-closed eyes and a yawn; a big smile; a downturned mouth and a tear; slanted eyebrows, a frown and a red face; wide eyes, a wavy mouth and a drop of sweat.

questions.explanation: 1 is yawning: cansado (tired). 2 smiles: contento (happy). 3 has a tear: triste (sad). 4 frowns with a red face: enojado (angry). 5 has wide eyes and sweat: nervioso (nervous). Enfermo (sick) and limpio (clean) aren't shown.

questions.stem: Type the missing form of estar: "¿Dónde ___ mis llaves?" (Where are my keys?)
questions.explanation: Llaves is plural, so the verb is the plural form of estar: ¿Dónde están mis llaves? Write the accent: están. (One key: ¿Dónde está mi llave?)

questions.stem: Which sentences need estar? Select all that apply.
choices: Mi casa ___ cerca de la universidad.
questions.explanation: Location (Mi casa está cerca…), a feeling (Hoy estoy muy nerviosa) and a condition right now (El café está frío) take estar. Origin (Mis abuelos son de Puebla) and a job (Tu hermano es ingeniero) take ser.

questions.stem: Match each sentence to the reason for its verb.
left: La clase es en el salón 4.
questions.explanation: estar: location (Estoy en el centro) and feelings (preocupados). ser: origin (de Canadá), job (maestra), and the place of an event (La clase es en…). An event's location is the one place-sentence that takes ser.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: My house is near the school.
questions.explanation: Location takes estar: Mi casa está cerca de la escuela. "Near" is cerca de; lejos de means "far from". Spanish also allows Cerca de la escuela está mi casa, which puts the place first for emphasis.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The soup is cold.
questions.explanation: The soup's temperature right now is a condition: estar. The adjective agrees with la sopa, so fría, not frío. La sopa está fría is the usual order; Está fría la sopa is also natural in speech.

questions.stem: Complete: "En la sala ___ un sofá y dos sillas."
questions.explanation: The sentence says that things exist in the room, introduced with un and a number, so it takes hay (there is / there are). Hay never changes, even for several things. "está/están" is for a known thing: El sofá está en la sala.

questions.stem: Complete: "Las llaves ___ encima de la mesa."
questions.explanation: Las llaves are particular, known keys, so the sentence says where they are: estar. They are plural, so están. "Hay las llaves" is never right: hay doesn't take el/la/los/las.

questions.stem: Complete: "El gato está al lado ___ sofá."
questions.explanation: El sofá is masculine, and de + el always joins into del: al lado del sofá. "de la" is for feminine nouns (al lado de la cama), and "de el" is never written as two words before a noun.

questions.stem: Your friend says: "La farmacia está enfrente de mi casa." Where is the pharmacy?
questions.explanation: Enfrente de means in front of or opposite, and with buildings it usually means across the street. Behind is detrás de, next to is al lado de, and inside would be en.

questions.stem: Read the ad: "Se renta departamento. Dos cuartos, un baño, cocina con estufa. No hay refrigerador. Cerca del metro. Renta: 8,500 pesos al mes." What is NOT in the apartment?
questions.explanation: No hay refrigerador: there's no fridge. The ad lists two bedrooms (dos cuartos), a bathroom (un baño) and a kitchen with a stove (estufa). The rent is 8,500 pesos a month.

questions.stem: Which question asks how many bedrooms there are?
questions.explanation: "How many … are there?" is ¿Cuántos … hay?, and cuántos agrees with cuartos (masculine plural). "Cuántas" is feminine. "están" asks where known things are, and ¿Dónde están los cuartos? means "Where are the bedrooms?"

questions.stem: In Mexico, which word means the apartment you rent?
questions.explanation: Mexico says el departamento (others say el apartamento). In Spain el piso is an apartment, but in Mexico el piso is a floor or storey. La sala is the living room, and la renta is the rent you pay.

questions.stem: Name the numbered rooms and parts of this house.

image.alt: A cross-section of a two-storey house. Six parts are numbered: 1 a room with a fridge and a stove, 2 a room with a table and chairs, 3 a sofa in a room downstairs, 4 a staircase, 5 a room upstairs with a bed, 6 a room upstairs with a toilet and a shower.

questions.explanation: 1 has the fridge and stove: la cocina. 2 has the table and chairs: el comedor. 3 has the sofa: la sala. 4 is la escalera (the stairs). 5, upstairs with the bed, is el cuarto, and 6, with the toilet and shower, is el baño.

questions.stem: Where is the cat in each picture? Choose the phrase for each number.

image.alt: Six small pictures of a cat, numbered 1 to 6: its head pokes out of an open box; it sits on top of a box; it sits under a table; it sits beside a box; only its ears and tail show behind a big box; it sits between two boxes.

questions.explanation: 1 en la caja (in the box), 2 encima de la caja (on top of the box), 3 debajo de la mesa (under the table), 4 al lado de la caja (next to the box), 5 detrás de la caja (behind the box), 6 entre las cajas (between the boxes).

questions.stem: Type the missing word: "El perro está debajo ___ la cama." (The dog is under the bed.)
questions.explanation: Debajo needs de before the noun: debajo de la cama. Encima de, al lado de, enfrente de and detrás de work the same way; only en and entre take no de.

questions.stem: Match each Mexican word to the word used in Spain.
questions.explanation: Mexico says el departamento, el refrigerador (or el refri), el clóset and rentar; Spain says el piso, la nevera, el armario and alquilar. La estufa is a trap: in Spain it means a heater, not a word for any of these.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Hay dos baños en la casa.
Hay el sofá en la sala.
Mi cama está en el cuarto.
Los libros está en la mesa.
questions.explanation: Hay goes with numbers and un/una (dos baños, una estufa), and a known thing with mi takes estar (Mi cama está…). "Hay el sofá" is wrong: hay doesn't take el. "Los libros está" needs the plural: están.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: There are two bathrooms in the house.
questions.explanation: "There are" is hay, which never changes: Hay dos baños en la casa. The place can also come first: En la casa hay dos baños. Están is for known things (Los baños están arriba: the bathrooms are upstairs).

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The fridge is next to the stove.
questions.explanation: A known thing (el refrigerador) takes estar. La estufa is feminine, so de la stays apart: al lado de la estufa. Al lado del is only for masculine nouns (al lado del sofá).

questions.stem: Complete: "Me ___ mucho los tacos."
questions.explanation: With gustar, the thing you like is the subject. Los tacos is plural, so the verb is plural: Me gustan los tacos. "gusta" is for one thing (Me gusta el taco), and "gusto" would mean "I please".

questions.stem: Complete: "A mis hijos les ___ cocinar y comer."
questions.explanation: Infinitives (cocinar, comer) always take the singular gusta, even when there are two of them, and even though the people (mis hijos) are plural. The verb agrees with the thing liked, not the person.

questions.stem: Your friend says: "No me gusta el pescado." You don't like fish either. What do you answer?
questions.explanation: After a negative sentence, agree with tampoco: A mí tampoco (me neither). "A mí también" agrees with a positive sentence. "A mí sí" disagrees (I do like it).

questions.stem: How do you say "We're very hungry"?
questions.explanation: Spanish says "to have hunger": tener hambre. Hambre is feminine (it only takes el because of the stressed a-), so "very" is mucha: Tenemos mucha hambre. Estar and ser don't work here.

questions.stem: Complete: "¿Ustedes ___ café o té?"
questions.explanation: Querer changes e to ie in every form except nosotros: quiero, quieres, quiere, queremos, quieren. Ustedes takes the ellos form: quieren. "queren" forgets the stem change, and "quiere" is singular.

questions.stem: You're in a café and want to order politely. What do you say?
choices: Quisiera un jugo de naranja, por favor.
Me gusta un jugo de naranja.
questions.explanation: Quisiera (I would like) is the polite way to order. "Me gusta…" says you like orange juice in general, not that you want one now. "Yo quiero" can sound blunt, and "jugo naranja" is missing de. "Tengo" means "I have".

questions.stem: A Mexican coworker asks: "¿A qué hora es la comida?" What is she asking about?
questions.explanation: In Mexico la comida means food, and also the main meal of the day, usually eaten in the early afternoon. Breakfast is el desayuno and dinner is la cena.

questions.stem: Read: "A mí me encanta la fruta, pero a mi hermano no le gusta. Él prefiere el pan con queso." Which is true?
questions.explanation: Me encanta la fruta: the writer loves fruit. The brother doesn't like it (no le gusta) and prefers bread with cheese (prefiere = prefers). So only the writer loves fruit.

questions.stem: Name the numbered foods and drinks on this Mexican table.

image.alt: A table with six numbered things: 1 a basket of flat round breads, 2 a bowl of brown beans, 3 a fried egg on a plate of rice, 4 a glass of orange juice, 5 a cup of coffee, 6 a bowl with a banana and an apple.

questions.explanation: 1 las tortillas, 2 los frijoles (beans), 3 el huevo (a fried egg, on rice), 4 el jugo (orange juice), 5 el café, 6 la fruta (a banana and an apple). There's no bread (el pan) or milk (la leche).

questions.stem: Type the right form of gustar: "¿Te ___ las papas?" (Do you like potatoes?)
questions.explanation: Las papas is plural, so the verb is gustan: ¿Te gustan las papas? The te shows who likes them (you); the verb agrees with the potatoes.

questions.stem: Match each pronoun to the person who likes the thing.
questions.explanation: me = (to) me, te = (to) you, nos = (to) us, les = (to) them or to you all. Le (not shown) is for él, ella or usted. "A usted y a mí" would be nos (us), not one of these.

questions.stem: Put the conversation at the table in order.
choices: Hay pollo con arroz. ¿Te gusta el pollo?
questions.explanation: First the question (Are you hungry?), then the answer and a new question (What is there to eat?), then the answer with a question about chicken, and last the reply: Sí, me encanta (Yes, I love it).

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: My dad likes coffee.
questions.explanation: A mi papá le gusta el café: a + the person, then le (to him), then gusta (singular, for one thing), then the thing liked with its article. Le gusta el café a mi papá is also correct. "me" would mean "to me".

questions.stem: Build the order in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I'd like a coffee with milk, please.
questions.explanation: Quisiera is the polite chunk for ordering, then what you want: un café con leche, por favor. Por favor can also come first: Por favor, quisiera un café con leche. "Me gusta" would say you like it in general, and "sin" means without.

questions.stem: How do you say 500 pesos?
questions.explanation: 500 is one of the three irregular hundreds: quinientos (also setecientos, 700, and novecientos, 900). Peso is masculine, so it stays quinientos, not quinientas.

questions.stem: Which is 150?
questions.explanation: Before another number, cien becomes ciento: ciento cincuenta. Y only goes between tens and units (cincuenta y cinco), never after the hundreds.

questions.stem: Complete: "¿Cuánto ___ los lentes?"
questions.explanation: The verb agrees with the thing that costs: los lentes is plural, so cuestan. Costar changes o to ue: cuesta, cuestan. "costan" forgets the stem change, and "cuesta" is for one thing.

questions.stem: Complete: "Esta tienda es ___ que esa; los precios son buenos y la gente es simpática."
questions.explanation: The comparative of bueno is mejor (better), with no más: Esta tienda es mejor que esa. "más mejor" doubles the comparison, and "tan buena" would need como, not que.

questions.stem: You want one more coffee. What do you say?
questions.explanation: Otro means another and never takes un in front: otro café. It agrees with the noun, and café is masculine, so otro, not otra.

questions.stem: Complete: "¿Cuánto cuesta ___ mochila?" (this backpack, the one you're holding)
questions.explanation: Demonstratives agree with the noun: la mochila is feminine, so esta mochila. "este" is masculine, "esto" is used without a noun (¿Qué es esto?), and "está" with an accent is the verb estar.

questions.stem: Read the dialogue: "—Son seiscientos cincuenta pesos. —Aquí tiene setecientos. —Y aquí está su cambio." How much change does the customer get?
questions.explanation: The price is 650 (seiscientos cincuenta) and the customer pays 700 (setecientos): 700 − 650 = 50 pesos of change (el cambio).

questions.stem: This price tag says 1,250.50 MXN. What does each numbered part show?

image.alt: A price tag for a backpack (Mochila) reading 1,250.50 MXN. Four lines point to the comma, the point, the 50 and the letters MXN, numbered 1 to 4.

questions.explanation: Mexico writes numbers like the US: the comma (1) separates thousands, and the point (2) separates pesos from centavos. 50 (3) are the centavos, and MXN (4) is the code for the Mexican peso. Say it: mil doscientos cincuenta pesos con cincuenta centavos.

questions.stem: Type the number 700 in Spanish words.
questions.explanation: 700 is setecientos, one of the three irregular hundreds (not sietecientos). Before a feminine noun it becomes setecientas: setecientas personas.

questions.stem: Match each price to how you say it.
questions.explanation: 1,500 = mil quinientos (never un mil), 115 = ciento quince, 900 = novecientos (irregular: not nuevecientos), 2,000 = dos mil (mil doesn't take a plural).

questions.stem: Put the prices in order, from the cheapest to the most expensive.
questions.explanation: doscientos cincuenta = 250, quinientos veinte = 520, setecientos = 700, mil cien = 1,100.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: El mercado es más barato que el supermercado.
Esta mochila es menos cara que esa.
Mi celular es más bueno que tu celular.
La mochila cuesta más de mil pesos.
Los tacos son tan ricos que las tortas.
questions.explanation: más/menos + adjective + que is right (más barato que, menos cara que), and before a number "more than" is más de (más de mil pesos). "más bueno" should be mejor, and tan goes with como: tan ricos como.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The market is cheaper than the supermarket.
questions.explanation: más + adjective + que: El mercado es más barato que el supermercado. What something is like takes ser, and como goes with tan, not más.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: This backpack costs six hundred pesos.
questions.explanation: One backpack, so the singular cuesta; mochila is feminine, so esta. Seis + cientos = seiscientos, a regular hundred.

questions.stem: In many Mexican families, which meal is the biggest of the day?
choices: El desayuno, early in the morning
La comida, in the early afternoon
questions.explanation: In a common Mexican pattern (a generalization: habits vary), la comida, often between about 2 and 4 pm, is the main meal, with several courses. La cena in the evening is often light. In Spain el almuerzo can be lunch, but in Mexico it's usually a mid-morning snack or late breakfast.

questions.stem: How do you say "a chicken taco" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Spanish puts the main thing first and joins the filling with de: un taco de pollo, like jugo de naranja. "del pollo" would mean the taco of a particular chicken.

questions.stem: You're shopping in a Mexico City market and want red tomatoes for a salad. What do you ask for?
questions.explanation: In central and southern Mexico the red tomato is el jitomate; el tomate or tomate verde is the small green tomatillo. Elotes are ears of corn, and aguacates are avocados.

questions.stem: Which is the most natural way to ask a server in a fonda for the check?
choices: Quiero pagar la cuenta ahora mismo.
questions.explanation: ¿Me trae la cuenta, por favor? (Could you bring me the check?) is polite, with usted. "Dame" uses tú and sounds rude to a stranger, "¿Puedo tener…?" is a word-for-word translation from English, and the last one sounds impatient.

questions.stem: At a taco stand the cook asks: "¿Para aquí o para llevar?" What does he want to know?
choices: Whether you pay in cash or by card
Whether you'll eat here or take the food away
questions.explanation: Para aquí = for here (to eat at the stand), para llevar = to go (to take away). Answer Para aquí or Para llevar.

questions.stem: You walk past a table where strangers are eating in a fonda. What is it common to say in Mexico?
questions.explanation: ¡Provecho! or ¡Buen provecho! (enjoy your meal) is commonly said to people who are eating, even strangers, and the usual reply is Gracias. Mucho gusto is for meeting someone, ¡Qué rico! means "how delicious", and ¡Salud! is a toast (or "bless you").

questions.stem: Your set lunch for two costs 380 pesos and you want to leave about 10 percent. Which tip is closest?
questions.explanation: 10 percent of 380 is 38 pesos; rounding to 40 is fine. About 10 to 15 percent is a common guide in Mexican restaurants, and Mexico's consumer agency, Profeco, says a tip is voluntary.

questions.stem: Read the menu board: "Comida corrida 120 pesos: sopa de verduras, arroz, guisado (pollo en salsa verde o carne con papas), agua del día." Which is true?
choices: You choose between chicken and meat for the main dish.
questions.explanation: The guisado (main dish) is pollo en salsa verde OR (o) carne con papas, so you choose one. The agua del día is included in the 120 pesos, and the set lunch starts with vegetable soup.

questions.stem: Name the numbered foods.

image.alt: Six foods on a table, numbered 1 to 6: a halved avocado with a pit, an ear of corn on a stick, two red tomatoes, three small green tomatillos with a papery husk, a stack of flat round corn breads, a clay bowl of red sauce.

questions.explanation: 1 el aguacate (avocado), 2 el elote (corn on the cob), 3 el jitomate (red tomato), 4 el tomate verde (tomatillo), 5 las tortillas, 6 la salsa (a spicy sauce). There are no chiles or beans in the picture.

questions.stem: Complete the order with the missing word: "¿Me da tres tacos ___ carne, por favor?"
questions.explanation: The filling is joined with de: tacos de carne, tacos de pollo, quesadilla de queso.

questions.stem: You want your food to go. Type the two-word answer to "¿Para aquí o para llevar?"
questions.explanation: Para llevar = to go, to take away. If you're eating there, answer Para aquí.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
choices: a corn-based snack such as a taco or a quesadilla
questions.explanation: Un antojito ("a little craving") is a snack such as a taco, quesadilla or sope. A fonda is a small, often family-run restaurant, where many people eat la comida corrida, the set lunch. La propina is the tip. The check is la cuenta.

questions.stem: Which of these Spanish words come from Nahuatl? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Aguacate (from ahuacatl), elote (from elotl) and jitomate (from xitomatl) are Nahuatl loanwords, like tomate and chile. Queso and pollo come from Latin.

questions.stem: Build the order in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Can I have a lime water, please?
questions.explanation: ¿Me da…? is the everyday way to order in Mexico: ¿Me da un agua de limón, por favor? Agua is feminine but takes un in the singular because of the stressed a- (un agua, el agua), so "una agua" is the trap. Por favor can also come first.

questions.stem: What is a tianguis?
choices: A market in a permanent building, open every day
A shop that sells only tortillas
A street market held on a fixed day of the week
questions.explanation: A tianguis (from Nahuatl tianquiztli, market) sets up in the street on a fixed day and is taken down in the evening. A permanent market building open every day is el mercado.

questions.stem: How do you ask for half a kilo of cheese?
choices: ¿Me da un medio kilo de queso?
questions.explanation: Medio takes no un and agrees with kilo (masculine): medio kilo. The quantity is joined to the food with de: medio kilo de queso.

questions.stem: The vendor says: "Las manzanas están a cuarenta el kilo." You ask for a quarter of a kilo. How much do you pay?
questions.explanation: Están a cuarenta el kilo = 40 pesos per kilo. A quarter (un cuarto de kilo) is 40 ÷ 4 = 10 pesos. Half a kilo would be 20.

questions.stem: Where is it usually NOT appropriate to bargain in Mexico?
choices: At a stall selling used goods
questions.explanation: Supermarkets, chain stores, pharmacies and shops with price tags have fixed prices; there you can only ask about an offer or a discount. Polite bargaining is often normal at craft, souvenir, clothes and used-goods stalls. (A generalization: practices vary.)

questions.stem: You like a bag (la bolsa) that costs 350 pesos. How do you bargain politely?
questions.explanation: ¿Me la deja en…? (Will you let me have it for…?) with la, because la bolsa is feminine. ¿Me lo deja…? is for a masculine thing; a vendor would understand it, but la is right here. The third sounds rude, and ¿Cuánto cuestan? only asks the price of several things.

questions.stem: A car ad says "210,000 pesos". How do you read it?
questions.explanation: 210,000 = 210 × 1,000 = doscientos diez mil. Mil has no plural (not miles), and the 210 comes before mil as one block.

questions.stem: Which is correct for 2,000,000 pesos?
questions.explanation: Millón is a noun: plural millones, and de when the thing counted comes right after it: dos millones de pesos (but dos millones trescientos mil pesos, with no de). "dos mil millones" is two billion.

questions.stem: Read the receipt. What does each numbered line show?

image.alt: A shop receipt from Abarrotes Doña Lupe in Puebla. Items: 1.000 KG JITOMATE 28.00; 0.500 KG QUESO OAXACA 95.00; 1 DOC HUEVO 42.00; 0.250 KG JAMON 38.50. Then TOTAL 203.50, EFECTIVO 250.00 and CAMBIO 46.50, each with the peso sign. Markers 1 to 3 are beside the total, efectivo and cambio amounts; markers 4 to 6 are beside the quantities 0.500 KG, 1 DOC and 0.250 KG.

choices: the cash the customer handed over
questions.explanation: TOTAL (1) is everything together, 203.50. EFECTIVO (2) is the cash handed over, 250.00, and CAMBIO (3) is the change, 46.50. 0.500 KG is medio kilo (4), 1 DOC is una docena (5), and 0.250 KG is un cuarto de kilo (6). There's no tip on a shop receipt.

questions.stem: You pay 100 pesos for something that costs 64.50. Type the change in figures (pesos.centavos).
questions.explanation: 100 − 64.50 = 35.50: treinta y cinco pesos con cincuenta centavos, or in quick speech treinta y cinco cincuenta.

questions.stem: Match each quantity to its amount.
questions.explanation: una docena = 12, media docena = 6, medio kilo = 500 grams (half of 1,000), un cuarto de kilo = 250 grams (a quarter of 1,000).

questions.stem: Put Lucía's conversation at the market stall in order.
questions.explanation: First ask the price (¿A cómo están…?), hear it (sixty a kilo), order (half a kilo), the vendor hands it over and asks if there's anything else, and you finish and ask how much you owe.

questions.stem: Which phrases are useful for paying and getting change? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: ¿Tiene cambio de quinientos? (Do you have change for 500?), ¿Cuánto le debo? (How much do I owe you?) and Aquí está su cambio (Here's your change) are all about paying. ¿Me lo deja en cien? is bargaining, and ¡Buen provecho! is said to people eating.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: A dozen eggs and half a kilo of cheese, please.
questions.explanation: Each quantity joins its food with de: una docena de huevos, medio kilo de queso. Medio takes no un, so "un medio kilo" is the trap. The two items can come in either order.

questions.stem: How do you say "It's one o'clock" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: One o'clock is singular: "Es la una." The article "la" stands for "la hora", so it is feminine and "uno" becomes "una". "Son" is only for the other hours.

questions.stem: Which sentence says 3:30?
questions.explanation: Every hour except one o'clock takes "son las": "Son las tres y media." The article can't be dropped, and "media" is feminine because it means half an hour (media hora).

questions.stem: Which is a natural way to say 2:45 in Mexico?
choices: Es un cuarto para las tres.
Es un cuarto para las dos.
questions.explanation: In Mexico you count to the next hour with "para": 2:45 is "un cuarto para las tres" (a quarter to three). "Son las tres menos cuarto" also works everywhere. "Las dos menos cuarto" is 1:45, "las tres y cuarto" is 3:15, and "un cuarto para las dos" is 1:45.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I work on Mondays"?
questions.explanation: Spanish uses the article instead of "on", with no "en": "los lunes" = on Mondays (every Monday), "el lunes" = on Monday (one). Days are written in lowercase.

questions.stem: Which is the standard way to say "at 7 a.m."?
choices: a la siete de la mañana
a las siete de la mañana
en las siete de la mañana
questions.explanation: "At" with a clock time is "a las" (or "a la una"), and after a clock time the part of the day takes "de la": "a las siete de la mañana". "De mañana" without "la" would mix in "tomorrow", and "en" is not used for clock times.

questions.stem: Look at the planner. When does she go to the gym?

image.alt: A weekly planner, Mi semana. lunes: trabajo, 9:00 a 17:00. martes: clase de español, 19:00. miércoles: trabajo; gimnasio, 18:30. jueves: clase de español, 19:00. viernes: trabajo hasta las 15:00; cena con Pablo, 20:30. sábado: mercado por la mañana. domingo: comida con mi familia, 14:00.

choices: el lunes a las seis y media
el miércoles a las seis y media de la tarde
el miércoles a las ocho y media de la noche
el jueves a las siete de la tarde
questions.explanation: The Wednesday (miércoles) row says "gimnasio, 18:30". In the 12-hour clock 18:30 is "las seis y media de la tarde". Thursday at 19:00 is her Spanish class.

questions.stem: Type the missing words: 8:30 = "Son las ocho ___."
questions.explanation: Half past is "y media": "Son las ocho y media." Reading the digits, "las ocho y treinta", is also correct.

questions.stem: Type the day that comes after "martes" (no article).
questions.explanation: The week goes lunes, martes, miércoles, jueves, viernes, sábado, domingo. "Miércoles" has a written accent on the first e (MYER-co-les).

questions.stem: Match each time to the Spanish.
questions.explanation: Up to half past, add minutes with "y": y cuarto (3:15), y media (3:30). After half past, count to the next hour with "menos": 3:45 is "las cuatro menos cuarto". "Las tres menos cuarto" is 2:45.

questions.stem: Say the time on each numbered clock.

image.alt: Four numbered clock faces showing 3:15, 3:30, 2:45 and 1:00.

choices: Es un cuarto para las tres.
questions.explanation: Clock 1 shows 3:15 (y cuarto), clock 2 shows 3:30 (y media), clock 3 shows 2:45, a quarter to three (un cuarto para las tres, or las tres menos cuarto), and clock 4 shows one o'clock, the only hour with "es".

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: "Hoy es martes" (no article after ser with today's day), "Trabajo el sábado" (on Saturday) and "Los domingos nunca trabajo" are all correct. Two o'clock is plural: "Son las dos." And there is no "en" before days: "Nos vemos el lunes."

questions.stem: Put these parts of the day in order, starting with la mañana.
questions.explanation: The day runs from la mañana (morning) to el mediodía (noon), then la tarde (afternoon, until it gets dark), la noche (night) and la medianoche (midnight), which ends the day.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I never work on Sundays.
questions.explanation: Nunca goes before the verb, with no "no": "Nunca trabajo los domingos." The time phrase can also come first: "Los domingos nunca trabajo."

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The class is at nine in the morning.
questions.explanation: "At nine" is "a las nueve", and after a clock time the part of the day takes "de la": "La clase es a las nueve de la mañana." Spanish also allows the time first: "A las nueve de la mañana es la clase."

questions.stem: Complete: "Yo ___ al cine esta noche."
questions.explanation: Ir is irregular: yo voy, tú vas, él va, nosotros vamos, ellos van. "Ir" is the infinitive and can't follow "yo" directly.

questions.stem: Complete with the standard written form: "¿___ vas el sábado? — Al museo."
questions.explanation: The answer "Al museo" names a destination, so the question is "¿Adónde vas?" (where to). "De dónde" asks where from, "cuándo" when and "cómo" how.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "We're going to eat in a restaurant"?
choices: Vamos a comemos en un restaurante.
Van a comer en un restaurante.
Vamos a comer en un restaurante.
questions.explanation: Ir a + infinitive: the form of ir (vamos), then a, then the infinitive (comer). The a can't be left out, the second verb stays in the infinitive, and "van" would be "they" or "you all".

questions.stem: Your friend calls from the kitchen: "¡Ana, ven!" What do you answer?
questions.explanation: Venir means moving toward the speaker. You are going toward your friend, so Spanish uses ir: "¡Ya voy!" (I'm coming!). "¡Ya vengo!" means I'll be back.

questions.stem: A friend asks "¿Quieres ir al teatro esta noche?" You can't go. What do you say?
choices: Lo siento, no puedo. Voy a estudiar.
questions.explanation: "Lo siento, no puedo" (I'm sorry, I can't) plus a short reason is the polite way to decline. The other three all accept the invitation.

questions.stem: Complete: "La gente ___ al parque los domingos."
questions.explanation: La gente (people) is grammatically singular in Spanish, so the verb is singular: "La gente va." English says "people go", which tempts learners to write "van".

questions.stem: Type the right form of ir: "Mis padres ___ a visitar el museo."
questions.explanation: Mis padres = ellos, so: van. Then a + infinitive: "Mis padres van a visitar el museo."

questions.stem: Type the missing word: "Vengo ___ gimnasio." (from the gym)
questions.explanation: From = de, and de + el always contracts to del: "Vengo del gimnasio." With a feminine noun there is no contraction: "Vengo de la fiesta."

questions.stem: Put the conversation in order.
choices: Lo siento, el sábado no puedo.
questions.explanation: The invitation comes first, then the refusal for Saturday, a new suggestion (Sunday), the acceptance with a question about the time, and finally the time.

questions.stem: Name the place in each numbered picture.

image.alt: Six numbered picture tiles: a film screen with seats, two theatre masks, a building with columns, a tree and a bench, a dumbbell, and a plate with a fork and knife.

questions.explanation: The screen is el cine, the masks el teatro, the building with columns el museo, the tree and bench el parque, the dumbbell el gimnasio and the plate el restaurante.

questions.stem: Match each person to the right form.
questions.explanation: Ir: voy, vas, va, vamos, van. Venir: vengo, vienes, viene, venimos, vienen. "Vas" is tú (ir) and "viene" is él (venir).

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Mañana voy a visitar a mi abuela.
questions.explanation: A + el must contract to al ("Voy al parque", not "a el"). With la there is no contraction: "a la cafetería", "de la fiesta". "Mañana voy a visitar a mi abuela" is ir a + infinitive, with a before a person.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I'm going to see a film tonight.
questions.explanation: Ir a + infinitive: "voy a ver". The time can go at the end or the start: "Voy a ver una película esta noche" or "Esta noche voy a ver una película."

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: We're going to the park together.
questions.explanation: "Vamos al parque juntos" (a + el = al). "Juntos" can also go right after the verb: "Vamos juntos al parque."

questions.stem: Complete: "Hoy no ___ ir a la fiesta." (poder, yo)
questions.explanation: Poder is an o → ue verb: puedo, puedes, puede, podemos, pueden. "Podo" forgets the change, "pudo" is a past form, and "podemos" is nosotros.

questions.stem: Complete: "Nosotros ___ fútbol los sábados." (jugar)
questions.explanation: The nosotros form never changes its stem: jugamos. The u → ue change happens only in yo, tú, él and ellos (juego, juegas, juega, juegan).

questions.stem: Complete: "¿Qué ___ tú, el café o el té?" (preferir)
questions.explanation: Preferir is e → ie, and only the last e of the stem changes: prefieres. "Prefieren" is the ellos form.

questions.stem: Which verb do you use with "la guitarra"?
questions.explanation: Instruments take tocar: "tocar la guitarra". Jugar is for games and sports (jugar fútbol).

questions.stem: Complete: "En el restaurante, yo siempre ___ tacos." (to order)
questions.explanation: To ask for or order something is pedir, an e → i verb: yo pido. "Preguntar" is to ask a question, and "pide" and "piden" are the él and ellos forms.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Empiezo a trabajar a las ocho.
Empezo a trabajar a las ocho.
Empiezo de trabajar a las ocho.
questions.explanation: Empezar is e → ie (empiezo) and takes a before an infinitive: "Empiezo a trabajar."

questions.stem: In the present tense, in which person does a stem-changing verb keep the vowel of the infinitive?
questions.explanation: In nosotros (and vosotros) the stress falls on the ending, so the stem doesn't change: queremos, podemos, pedimos. The other four forms change: the "boot".

questions.stem: Type the right form of dormir: "Mi hijo ___ diez horas."
questions.explanation: Dormir is o → ue, and mi hijo is él: duerme.

questions.stem: Type the yo form of volver: "___ a casa a las seis."
questions.explanation: Volver is o → ue: vuelvo, vuelves, vuelve, volvemos, vuelven.

questions.stem: Match each infinitive to its yo form.
questions.explanation: e → ie: pienso, entiendo; o → ue: puedo; e → i: pido; u → ue: juego. "Penso" and "jugo" forget the stem change (and "jugo" is the word for juice).

questions.stem: What activity does each numbered picture show?

image.alt: Six numbered picture tiles: a soccer ball in front of a goal, a baseball bat and ball, a basketball hoop and ball, a swimmer in waves, a guitar, and a bicycle.

questions.explanation: The goal is fútbol, the bat béisbol, the hoop básquetbol, the waves nadar, the guitar tocar la guitarra (tocar for instruments) and the bicycle andar en bicicleta.

questions.stem: Which of these verbs change their stem in the present? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Dormir (duermo), cerrar (cierro) and pedir (pido) are stem-changing verbs. Nadar (nado) and cantar (canto) are regular.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: My sister plays the guitar very well.
questions.explanation: Instruments take tocar: "Mi hermana toca la guitarra muy bien." "Muy bien" may also come before the object: "Mi hermana toca muy bien la guitarra."

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I prefer to swim in the morning.
questions.explanation: Preferir + infinitive, with the e → ie change in yo: "Prefiero nadar por la mañana." The time can also open the sentence: "Por la mañana prefiero nadar."

questions.stem: Complete: "Yo ___ a las seis." (levantarse)
questions.explanation: The reflexive pronoun matches the subject: yo → me, and the verb is in the yo form: "Me levanto." Without "me", "levanto" means "I lift (something)".

questions.stem: Complete: "¿A qué hora ___ tus hijos?" (acostarse)
questions.explanation: Tus hijos = ellos, so the pronoun is se, and acostarse is o → ue in the ellos form: se acuestan. "Te acuestas" is tú, and "acuestan" has lost its pronoun.

questions.stem: Which sentence is NOT correct?
questions.explanation: With ir a + infinitive the pronoun goes on the end of the infinitive (voy a bañarme) or before the conjugated verb (me voy a bañar), never in between.

questions.stem: Complete: "Todos los días ___ de casa a las siete." (salir, yo)
questions.explanation: Salir has an irregular yo form with g: salgo. The other persons are regular: sales, sale, salimos, salen.

questions.stem: Complete: "No ___ dónde está el museo." (saber, yo)
questions.explanation: The yo form of saber is sé, with an accent. Without the accent, se is the reflexive pronoun. "Sabo" doesn't exist.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: With body parts Spanish uses the article, not a possessive, because "me" already shows whose: "Me lavo los dientes." The pronoun goes before the verb, and "dientes" is plural, so "los".

questions.stem: Complete: "Después de ___, desayuno."
questions.explanation: After "después de" or "antes de" Spanish uses the infinitive, with the pronoun attached and matching the subject (yo → me): "Después de bañarme, desayuno."

questions.stem: Type the yo form of hacer: "Los domingos ___ la comida para toda la semana."
questions.explanation: Hacer has an irregular yo form: hago. The rest are regular: haces, hace, hacemos, hacen.

questions.stem: Type the missing pronoun: "Mis padres ___ levantan a las seis."
questions.explanation: Mis padres = ellos, and the reflexive pronoun for ellos (and ustedes) is se: "Mis padres se levantan a las seis."

questions.stem: Put Valeria's day in order.
questions.explanation: She wakes up, gets up, showers, leaves home and finally goes to bed: primero, luego, después, más tarde, finalmente.

questions.stem: What is Valeria doing in each numbered panel?

image.alt: Six numbered panels with clock times: 6:00 a woman in bed next to a ringing alarm clock; 6:30 a woman under a shower; 6:45 a woman reaching for a jacket; 7:10 a woman walking out of a door; 21:00 a woman washing dishes at a sink; 23:00 a woman asleep in bed with the moon in the window.

questions.explanation: 6:00 se despierta (wakes up), 6:30 se baña (showers), 6:45 se viste (gets dressed), 7:10 sale de casa (leaves home), 21:00 lava los platos (washes the dishes), 23:00 se acuesta (goes to bed).

questions.stem: Match each sentence to its meaning.
questions.explanation: Lavarse is washing yourself, lavar is washing something else. Irse (me voy) is to leave, quedarse to stay, and poner la mesa to set the table. "I go home" would be "Voy a casa".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Tomorrow I'm going to get up early.
questions.explanation: The pronoun is attached to the infinitive: "Mañana voy a levantarme temprano." "Mañana" can also go at the end: "Voy a levantarme temprano mañana."

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: First I shower and then I get dressed.
questions.explanation: "Primero me baño y luego me visto." ("Me baño primero y luego me visto" is also correct.) Sequence words come at the start of each part, and each reflexive verb carries its own pronoun.

questions.stem: In Mexico someone says "Ahorita llegó Carlos." What does it mean?
choices: Carlos is going to arrive later.
questions.explanation: The verb "llegó" is in the past, so "ahorita" points to a moment just before now: Carlos arrived a moment ago. Check the verb first.

questions.stem: You need to say clearly that you will do something "right now". Which expression is clearest?
questions.explanation: "Ahora mismo" means right now, this minute. "Ahorita" can mean now or later depending on context, "al rato" is in a while, and "más tarde" is later.

questions.stem: How would most people say 18:45 in conversation?
choices: las seis y cuarenta y cinco de la mañana
las ocho menos cuarto de la noche
un cuarto para las siete de la tarde
un cuarto para las seis de la tarde
questions.explanation: 18 − 12 = 6, so it is 6:45 p.m. Counting to the next hour gives "un cuarto para las siete de la tarde" (or "las siete menos cuarto"). "Un cuarto para las seis" would be 5:45.

questions.stem: According to the lesson's general guide for Mexico, which statement is the best advice?
choices: Business meetings usually start an hour late.
Guests at a home party should arrive 15 minutes early.
Government offices expect people to arrive late.
Arrive on time for a job interview, but you can ask whether a party starts en punto.
questions.explanation: As a generalization, work and official appointments are expected to start on time, while social invitations are looser in many places. Asking "¿en punto?" is the safe way to check.

questions.stem: Look at the sign. Can you make a payment there on Saturday at 11:00?

image.alt: A shop door sign: Horario de atención. Lunes a viernes: 9:00 a 18:00 h. Sábados: 10:00 a 14:00 h. Domingos y días festivos: cerrado. Note: Pagos y trámites solo en días hábiles.

choices: Yes, it is open from 10:00 to 14:00.
No, payments are only made on working days (días hábiles).
No, it is closed all day on Saturdays.
questions.explanation: The office is open on Saturdays from 10:00 to 14:00, but the note says "Pagos y trámites solo en días hábiles". A día hábil is a working day, Monday to Friday, so no payments on Saturday.

questions.stem: Complete: "El metro pasa ___ cinco minutos."
questions.explanation: Cada (every, each) never changes: "cada cinco minutos". With todos you'd need "todos los" (and with minutes that sounds odd); "cadas" doesn't exist.

questions.stem: Read: "Línea 3. Lunes a viernes: cada 12 minutos, de 6:00 a 22:00 h. Domingos: cada 20 minutos, de 8:00 a 21:00 h." ¿A qué hora sale el primer camión el domingo?
questions.explanation: The Sunday line says "de 8:00 a 21:00 h", so the first bus leaves at eight. Six o'clock is the first bus on weekdays.

questions.stem: In Mexico, what is "la hora pico"?
questions.explanation: La hora pico is rush hour, when buses and the metro are full. Spain says "la hora punta".

questions.stem: Write 15:10 in everyday Spanish: "Son las ___ y diez de la tarde."
questions.explanation: 15 − 12 = 3, and it's afternoon: "Son las tres y diez de la tarde."

questions.stem: Type the missing word: "Su tarjeta llega en cinco días ___." (working days)
questions.explanation: El día hábil = a working day; the plural is días hábiles, with the accent on the first a.

questions.stem: Match each expression to its meaning.
questions.explanation: Ahora mismo is the clearest "right now"; en un momento is in a moment; al rato is in a while; luego luego is a Mexican "right away". None of them means never, though a vague ahorita sometimes ends up that way.

questions.stem: Put these times in order, from earliest to latest in the day.
Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The meeting starts at nine sharp.
questions.explanation: "En punto" (sharp) follows the time: "La reunión empieza a las nueve en punto." The time can also open the sentence: "A las nueve en punto empieza la reunión" (or "… la reunión empieza").

questions.stem: Which sentences use cada correctly? Select all that apply.
choices: El camión pasa cada diez minutos.
Cada semanas visito a mi abuela.
questions.explanation: Cada never changes and takes a singular noun (cada lunes, cada semana) or a number + plural noun (cada diez minutos, cada dos horas). "Cada semanas" and "cadas día" are wrong.

questions.stem: Complete: "Diego ___ la trompeta en un mariachi."
questions.explanation: Instruments take tocar: "Diego toca la trompeta." Jugar is for sports and games.

questions.stem: According to the Spanish Academy's guide, which form is NOT considered good usage?
questions.explanation: Jugar al fútbol is standard everywhere, and jugar fútbol is accepted as valid in Latin American Spanish. Jugar a fútbol (a without the article) is heard mainly in Spain among Catalan speakers and is not considered good usage.

questions.stem: In Mexico, what does "¿A qué equipo le vas?" mean?
choices: Which team are you going to play for?
questions.explanation: Irle a un equipo is a Mexican way to say you support a team: "Le voy al América" = I support América.

questions.stem: Where does mariachi come from?
questions.explanation: Mariachi comes from west-central Mexico, above all Jalisco. Son jarocho is from southern Veracruz, cumbia from Colombia's Caribbean coast, and salsa grew in New York.

questions.stem: Where does cumbia come from?
questions.explanation: Cumbia comes from Colombia's Caribbean coast, usually described as a mix of Indigenous, African and Spanish roots. It later became hugely popular in Mexico, Peru and Argentina.

questions.stem: Read: "El sábado los Tigres juegan contra el América. En el minuto 30, el América mete un gol. En el minuto 60 y en el minuto 85, los Tigres meten dos goles." ¿Cómo termina el partido?
choices: Uno a cero para el América.
Dos a uno para los Tigres.
Dos a cero para los Tigres.
questions.explanation: América scores once (minute 30) and the Tigres twice (minutes 60 and 85), so it ends two-one to the Tigres: "dos a uno".

questions.stem: What is the word for a female player?
questions.explanation: Nouns in -or add -a for a woman: el jugador → la jugadora (like el vendedor → la vendedora). Compare la cantante, which doesn't change.

questions.stem: Read: "Sábado, 21:00 h: Salsa en el Club Caribe. Entrada: 200 MXN. Domingo, 13:00 h: Son jarocho en la plaza. Entrada libre." Which event is free?
questions.explanation: "Entrada libre" means free admission, and it's on the Sunday son jarocho. The salsa night costs 200 pesos.

questions.stem: Name each numbered instrument.

image.alt: Four numbered instruments: a trumpet, a violin with its bow, a drum with two sticks, and a guitar.

questions.explanation: 1 is la trompeta (trumpet), 2 el violín with its bow, 3 el tambor (drum) with sticks and 4 la guitarra. The guitarrón is the large bass guitar of a mariachi group.

questions.stem: Type the plural of "el gol".
questions.explanation: Gol ends in a consonant, so it adds -es: los goles.

questions.stem: Match each style to where it comes from.
questions.explanation: Mariachi: west-central Mexico, mainly Jalisco. Son jarocho: southern Veracruz. Cumbia: Colombia's Caribbean coast. Salsa: New York, built by Cuban and Puerto Rican musicians on Cuban son.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Tocar goes with instruments (toco el violín), jugar with sports (juego béisbol, juega al fútbol). "Juego la guitarra" and "toco fútbol" mix them up.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The fans sing in the stadium.
questions.explanation: "Los aficionados cantan en el estadio." The place can also come first: "En el estadio los aficionados cantan" or "En el estadio cantan los aficionados", and with the verb first, "Cantan los aficionados en el estadio."

questions.stem: In Mexico, which syllable of "beisbol" is usually stressed?
choices: it changes from sentence to sentence
questions.explanation: In Mexico (and several other countries) the word is said beis-BOL and written without an accent. Elsewhere it's béisbol, stressed on the first syllable, written with an accent.

questions.stem: A woman gives you directions (she uses usted with you). Complete: "___ derecho dos cuadras."
questions.explanation: The usted command comes from the yo form: sigo → drop -o → sig- + -a (an -ir verb) = siga. Sigue is the tú command, sigo means "I follow", and the infinitive seguir is not a command.

questions.stem: You tell a friend how to get to your place. Complete: "___ el metro hasta la estación Hidalgo."
questions.explanation: For a friend (tú), the command is the él form of the present: toma. Tome is the usted command, tomas is a statement ("you take"), and tomar is the infinitive.

questions.stem: You tell your friend to go out through the main door. Which tú command is correct? "___ por la puerta principal."
questions.explanation: Salir is one of the eight verbs with a short irregular tú command: sal. Sale is the él form (he goes out), salga is the usted command, and sales is a statement.

questions.stem: Which is the usted command of "cruzar"? "___ la avenida en el semáforo."
questions.explanation: From the yo form cruzo, drop -o and add -e: cruz- + e. Before e, z is written c, so the command is cruce. Cruze is a misspelling, cruza is the tú command and cruzo means "I cross".

questions.stem: Look at the map. You are at the red star. Someone says: "Siga derecho por la Avenida Juárez dos cuadras. En el semáforo, doble a la derecha." What is right there on your left after you turn?

image.alt: The street map from the lesson: Avenida Juárez crosses Calle Zaragoza, Hidalgo, Morelos and Allende. The red star is at Zaragoza and Juárez. The traffic light is on the corner of Morelos. North of the avenue are the bus stop, the church and square, and the pharmacy; south of it are the metro, a tall building, the bank on the corner of Morelos and the hospital behind it.

questions.explanation: Two blocks east from the star bring you to Calle Morelos, where the traffic light is. Turning right there, you walk south on Morelos, so your left is the east side of the street: the bank, on the corner (and the hospital behind it). The tall building is on your right, and the church and the pharmacy are north of the avenue.

questions.stem: What does "Siga derecho" mean?
questions.explanation: Derecho (with -o, no article) means straight ahead, so Siga derecho is "keep going straight ahead". Turn right is Doble a la derecha: derecha with -a and the article la.

questions.stem: You ask: "Disculpe, ¿hay un banco cerca de aquí?" Which answer fits?
choices: Sí, mire, está a dos cuadras, en la esquina.
Sí, me gusta mucho el banco.
questions.explanation: You asked whether there is a bank nearby, so the answer gives a place: "Yes, look, it's two blocks away, on the corner." The other answers say yes or no but talk about something else.

questions.stem: The receptionist tells you (usted) to make an appointment. Write the usted command of "hacer": "___ una cita, por favor." (Give only the verb.)
questions.explanation: Start from the irregular yo form hago, drop -o and add -a (hacer is an -er verb): haga. The irregular yo form carries into the command, just like tengo → tenga and salgo → salga. Haz is the tú command.

questions.stem: Match each verb to its tú command.
questions.explanation: These are five of the eight short irregular tú commands: ten, ven, pon, ve, haz (the others are di, sal, sé). Tiene is the regular él form, which these verbs don't use as a command, and vaya is the usted command of ir.

questions.stem: You give directions to a stranger (usted). Which commands are correct? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Doble (from doblo), cruce (cruzo, with z → c) and vaya (the irregular usted command of ir) are correct. Toma is the tú command; for usted it's tome. Llege is a misspelling: to keep the hard g sound before e, write llegue.

questions.stem: Name the numbered places on this street map.

image.alt: The street map from the lesson without the place names. Six places are numbered: a building with a tower and a cross, a traffic light on a street corner, a narrow building with a green cross, a building with columns and a coin, a building with a blue H sign, and the road over the river.

questions.explanation: The tower with a cross is la iglesia (church); the three lights on a pole are el semáforo (traffic light); the green cross marks la farmacia; the columns and coin show el banco; the H sign is el hospital; and the road over the river is el puente (bridge). The bus stop (la parada) is on the map but not numbered, and there is no school.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Turn left at the traffic light. (to a stranger)
questions.explanation: With a stranger, use the usted command doble (from doblo). The place phrase can come at the end or the start: Doble a la izquierda en el semáforo, or En el semáforo, doble a la izquierda (Doble en el semáforo a la izquierda is also accepted).

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Keep going straight ahead for two blocks. (to a friend)
questions.explanation: To a friend, the tú command is the él form of the present: sigue (siga is for usted). Sigue derecho dos cuadras is the most usual order; Sigue dos cuadras derecho is also fine.

questions.stem: Complete: "Voy a Oaxaca ___ autobús."
questions.explanation: To say how you travel, use en + the vehicle, with no article: en autobús, en avión, en tren. Por autobús is an English-style mistake; a is only for a pie (on foot).

questions.stem: Complete: "Conozco ___ tu hermano."
questions.explanation: Tu hermano is a specific person and the direct object of conocer, so Spanish puts the personal a in front: Conozco a tu hermano. Al would need the article el (al = a + el), and here the word before hermano is tu.

questions.stem: Complete: "Perdón, no ___ dónde está la estación."
questions.explanation: Knowing a fact, here where something is, takes saber: No sé dónde está. Conocer is for people and places you know from experience (No conozco la ciudad).

questions.stem: At the bus station you ask for "the bus to Puebla". Which is correct?
questions.explanation: Para gives the destination: el camión para Puebla is the bus going to Puebla. El camión de Puebla would be the bus from Puebla; en Puebla means in Puebla; por is not used for a destination.

questions.stem: Look at the ticket. At what time does the bus arrive in Puebla?

image.alt: The invented bus ticket from the lesson: Origen Ciudad de México (TAPO), Destino Puebla, Fecha 15/03/2026, Salida 08:30, Llegada 10:45, Asiento 23, Pasajero Ana López, Precio 320.00 MXN.

questions.explanation: La llegada is the arrival: 10:45. La salida (08:30) is the departure. 15/03 is the date (the 15th of March) and 23 is the seat (el asiento).

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: Esperar already means "to wait for", so no extra word is needed: Espero el camión. A bus is a thing, not a person, so there's no personal a either (and a el would always be al).

questions.stem: At a hotel, you say you have a reservation and the receptionist asks: "¿A nombre de quién?" Which answer fits?
questions.explanation: ¿A nombre de quién? means "In whose name?", so you give your name: A nombre de Ana López. Para dos noches answers "for how long", and the third floor is where the room is.

questions.stem: Write the yo form of "conocer": "No ___ Guadalajara, pero quiero ir." (Give only the verb.)
questions.explanation: Conocer is irregular only in the yo form: conozco (conoces, conoce, conocemos, conocen). In Latin America the z and c both sound like s: co-NOS-co.

questions.stem: Match each Spanish word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: el boleto = ticket (Spain: el billete), la maleta = suitcase, la llegada = arrival (departure is la salida), la habitación = a room in a hotel, el pasaporte = passport. Beach is la playa.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Conozco a tu mamá and Visito a mis abuelos need the personal a, because the objects are people. Subimos al tren (a + el) is correct. Cancún is a place, so no a: Conozco Cancún. On foot is a pie, not en pie.

questions.stem: Five field names are missing from this ticket. Name each numbered field.

image.alt: The invented bus ticket without five of its field names. Numbered values: Ciudad de México (TAPO), Puebla, 08:30, 10:45 and 23. The fields Fecha, Pasajero and Precio still have their names; the stub on the right repeats 23 and 08:30 without names.

questions.explanation: The trip starts in Mexico City (el origen) and goes to Puebla (el destino). The bus leaves at 08:30 (la salida) and arrives at 10:45 (la llegada); 23 is the seat (el asiento). The price and the date still have their labels.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I'm going to the station to buy the tickets.
questions.explanation: Para + infinitive gives the purpose ("in order to"): Voy a la estación para comprar los boletos. Por comprar doesn't express purpose here. The purpose can also come first: Para comprar los boletos, voy a la estación.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: We get on the train at seven.
questions.explanation: Subir (to get on) takes a: subir a + el tren = subir al tren. The time can go at the end or at the start: Subimos al tren a las siete, or A las siete subimos al tren.

questions.stem: How do you write "May 5th" in a Spanish sentence?
questions.explanation: A date is el + number + de + month, with the month in lowercase: el 5 de mayo. Mayo 5 follows English order, Mayo with a capital is wrong inside a sentence, and Spanish has no word for "on" before a date.

questions.stem: How do most Mexicans say "January 1st"?
questions.explanation: In Mexico and most of Latin America the first day of the month takes the ordinal: el primero de enero. El uno de enero is usual in Spain. Primer is used only directly before a masculine noun (el primer día).

questions.stem: Complete: "Hoy hace ___ calor."
questions.explanation: Calor is a masculine noun (el calor), so "very hot" is literally "much heat": Hace mucho calor. Muy goes with adjectives, not nouns, and mucha / muchos don't agree with el calor.

questions.stem: How do you say "It's raining"?
questions.explanation: Llover is an impersonal verb: just the él form llueve (o → ue), with no subject. (Está lloviendo is also heard, as a chunk.) Rain doesn't take hace, and es / está don't go with the verb llueve.

questions.stem: Look at the calendar. On what day of the week is el 10 de mayo de 2026?

image.alt: A calendar page for May 2026 with the weekdays lunes to domingo across the top; the 1st is a Friday. Marked days: 1 Día del Trabajo, 5 Batalla de Puebla, 10 Día de las Madres, 23 cumpleaños de Ana.

questions.explanation: The 1st is a Friday (viernes), so the 3rd and the 10th are Sundays: el 10 de mayo is domingo. In Mexico, Mother's Day is always on 10 May, whatever the weekday.

questions.stem: How do you read the year 1999?
questions.explanation: Spanish reads years as whole numbers: mil (1000) novecientos (900) noventa y nueve (99). Reading in pairs (diecinueve noventa y nueve) is English style; novecientos is one word, and 31–99 need y.

questions.stem: You are outside in winter and you feel cold. What do you say?
questions.explanation: A person "has" cold: Tengo frío. Hace frío describes the weather, not how you feel; estoy frío or soy frío would describe your body or your personality as cold.

questions.stem: Write the month: "La Navidad es el 25 de ___."
questions.explanation: Christmas is on 25 December: el 25 de diciembre. Months are written with a small letter.

questions.stem: Match each sentence to its meaning.
questions.explanation: Hace + noun: hace sol (sunny), hace viento (windy); the weather verbs llueve (rain) and nieva (snow); and estar + adjective for está nublado (cloudy). Hot and cold would be hace calor and hace frío.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Hoy es el primero de junio.
Mi cumpleaños es en el 3 de abril.
questions.explanation: Hace mucho frío, Nieva en las montañas and Hoy es el primero de junio are correct. A date takes no "on": Mi cumpleaños es el 3 de abril. With the noun calor, "very" is mucho: Hace mucho calor.

questions.stem: Choose the weather sentence for each numbered picture.

image.alt: Six weather pictures without captions: a sun; a cloud with rain; a cloud with snowflakes; three curling lines of wind; two grey clouds; a thermometer with low blue mercury and a snowflake. Each is numbered.

questions.explanation: Sun: Hace sol. Rain: Llueve. Snowflakes: Nieva. Wind lines: Hace viento. Clouds only: Está nublado. The low thermometer and the snowflake: Hace frío. A hot day (Hace calor) would show a high thermometer.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: In August it rains a lot.
questions.explanation: Llueve needs no subject, and "a lot" after a verb is mucho (muy only goes before adjectives and adverbs). The time phrase can start or end the sentence: En agosto llueve mucho / Llueve mucho en agosto.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: My birthday is on the first of May.
questions.explanation: A date needs no word for "on": Mi cumpleaños es el primero de mayo (Latin America uses primero for the 1st). El primero de mayo es mi cumpleaños is also correct.

questions.stem: Complete: "Me ___ los pies."
questions.explanation: Doler works like gustar: the thing that hurts is the subject. Los pies is plural, so the verb is plural: me duelen los pies. Duele is for one thing (me duele el pie).

questions.stem: How do you say "My head hurts"?
questions.explanation: Spanish shows the person with me and uses the article with body parts: Me duele la cabeza. Mi cabeza duele copies English, me duele mi cabeza adds an unnecessary "my", and the person is never the subject of doler.

questions.stem: What does "Hay que tomar mucha agua" mean?
choices: There is a lot of water.
I want a lot of water.
He has a lot of water.
You have to drink lots of water (everyone does).
questions.explanation: Hay que + infinitive is a general rule for everyone: "one must, you have to". Tomar is the everyday Mexican verb for "to drink". "There is a lot of water" would be Hay mucha agua, with no que and no verb.

questions.stem: It's very cold today. Your friend asks: "¿Qué llevas?" Which answer makes most sense?
choices: Llevo una chamarra y un suéter.
Llevo una playera y una falda corta.
Llevo los tenis en la mano.
questions.explanation: On a cold day you wear warm clothes: a jacket (la chamarra) and a sweater (el suéter). A T-shirt and a short skirt or a summer dress are for hot weather, and carrying your sneakers doesn't keep you warm.

questions.stem: Your friend has the flu. What do you say?
questions.explanation: To a friend (tú): ¡Que te mejores! — Get well soon. ¡Que se mejore! is the same wish for someone you call usted.

questions.stem: Complete: "Antes de comer, me lavo ___ manos."
questions.explanation: With body parts Spanish uses the article, not "my": me lavo las manos. Mano is feminine (la mano, las manos), so los is wrong too.

questions.stem: Read: "Hola, Paco. Hoy no voy a la clase: tengo gripa y me duelen la cabeza y la espalda. La doctora dice que tengo que descansar." Why isn't Laura going to class?
choices: She has the flu and has to rest.
questions.explanation: Tengo gripa = I have the flu; tengo que descansar = I have to rest. Her head and back hurt (me duelen la cabeza y la espalda). Nothing in the message says she has to work or is on vacation.

questions.stem: "¿Qué te duele?" — "Me ___ el estómago." (Give only the verb.)
questions.explanation: El estómago is one thing, so the verb is singular: me duele el estómago (I have a stomach ache). For several things it would be duelen.

questions.stem: Match each Mexican word to the word used in Spain.
questions.explanation: T-shirt: la playera (Mexico) / la camiseta (Spain). Jacket: la chamarra / la chaqueta. Sneakers: los tenis / las zapatillas. Sweater: el suéter / el jersey. La falda (skirt) and el vestido (dress) are the same in both.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: A mi papá le duele la espalda.
questions.explanation: Me duelen las piernas (plural, duelen), Tienes que descansar, Hay que hacer una cita and A mi papá le duele la espalda are all correct. Use the article with body parts: me lavo las manos. Los ojos is plural, so: me duelen los ojos.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of the body.

image.alt: A person standing, seen from the front, wearing a tank top and shorts. Six parts are numbered: the top of the head, an eye, an ear, the mouth, a hand and a foot.

questions.explanation: From the top: la cabeza (head), el ojo (eye), la oreja (ear), la boca (mouth), la mano (hand, feminine) and el pie (foot). The back (la espalda) can't be seen from the front, and the stomach is not numbered.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: You have to rest at home. (to a friend)
questions.explanation: For a particular person, use tener que + infinitive: Tienes que descansar en casa. Hay que is a general rule for everybody, with no person. En casa can also start the sentence.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Today I'm wearing a blue T-shirt.
questions.explanation: Llevar means to wear; the colour follows the noun: una playera azul. Hoy can start or end the sentence: Hoy llevo una playera azul / Llevo una playera azul hoy.

questions.stem: Look at the diagram. You are at Chapultepec and want to go to Pino Suárez on line 1. Which sign do you follow?

image.alt: The simplified metro diagram from the lesson. Line 1 (pink) runs from Observatorio on the left through Chapultepec, Insurgentes, Balderas, Salto del Agua and Pino Suárez to Pantitlán on the right. Line 2 (blue) runs from Cuatro Caminos through Revolución, Hidalgo, Bellas Artes, Allende, Zócalo/Tenochtitlan, Pino Suárez and San Antonio Abad to Tasqueña. Line 3 (olive) runs from Indios Verdes through Hidalgo, Juárez, Balderas and Centro Médico to Universidad.

questions.explanation: Pino Suárez is to the right of Chapultepec on line 1, towards the end station Pantitlán, so you follow Dirección Pantitlán. Observatorio is the other end of line 1; Tasqueña and Universidad are ends of lines 2 and 3.

questions.stem: Look at the diagram. At Pino Suárez you change to line 2 to go one stop to Zócalo/Tenochtitlan. Which direction do you take?

image.alt: The simplified metro diagram from the lesson, with lines 1, 2 and 3 in the city centre and the end stations of each line.

questions.explanation: On line 2, Zócalo/Tenochtitlan is the next station after Pino Suárez towards Cuatro Caminos. Dirección Tasqueña goes the other way (to San Antonio Abad), and Pantitlán and Indios Verdes are ends of lines 1 and 3.

questions.stem: In a Mexico City metro station you see the sign "Correspondencia Línea 3". What does it show?
choices: The way to change to line 3
The platform for women and children
questions.explanation: Correspondencia means a transfer to another line, so the sign shows the way to line 3. The exit is Salida.

questions.stem: On the diagram, how many stops is it on line 3 from Balderas to Hidalgo?

image.alt: The simplified metro diagram from the lesson. On line 3, going up from Balderas, the stations are Juárez and then Hidalgo.

questions.explanation: From Balderas, line 3 towards Indios Verdes stops at Juárez and then Hidalgo: two stops.

questions.stem: How do you usually pay on a pesero or a combi?
choices: With the MI card at a turnstile
At a ticket office in the station
questions.explanation: Peseros and combis are privately run: you pay the driver in cash when you get on. The MI card is used in the metro and on the Metrobús.

questions.stem: You want to take a long-distance bus from Mexico City to Puebla. Which bus station do you go to?
questions.explanation: Puebla is east of Mexico City, and buses to the east and south-east leave from the Terminal de Oriente, TAPO. Taxqueña serves the south, Observatorio the west and the Terminal del Norte the north.

questions.stem: In the address "Calle Fresno 27, Int. 4", what is the 4?
choices: the number of the flat or office inside the building
questions.explanation: Int. is short for número interior: the flat or office inside the building at number 27 (the número exterior). The postcode comes after C.P.

questions.stem: You give a taxi driver a street and number. He asks: "¿En qué colonia?" What does he want to know?
choices: Which neighbourhood the street is in
Which city you are going to
questions.explanation: La colonia is the named district in every Mexican address. Many cities have several streets with the same name in different colonias, so drivers always ask.

questions.stem: You are on a bus and want to ask where to get off for the museum. What do you say?
questions.explanation: ¿Dónde me bajo? asks where to get off. ¿Cuánto es el pasaje? asks the fare, and the other two ask whether the bus goes to or past the museum, which you already know if you're on it.

questions.stem: Write the word used on Mexico City metro signs for a transfer between two lines: "En Pino Suárez hay ___ con la línea 2."
questions.explanation: Correspondencia is the word on the signs at transfer stations. In everyday speech people also say hacer transbordo.

questions.stem: Match each abbreviation in a Mexican address to what it stands for.
questions.explanation: Col. = colonia (the district), C.P. = código postal, Int. = número interior (flat or office), S/N = sin número (no number), esq. = esquina (corner).

questions.stem: Which statements about the Mexico City metro are true, according to the lesson (checked November 2026)? Select all that apply.
choices: One fare covers any trip, even with changes of line.
Directions are named after the last station of the line.
Each line has a number or a letter and a colour.
The fare depends on how far you travel.
Signs say Norte or Sur to show the direction.
questions.explanation: There is one flat fare (5 pesos through 2026, per the city government), however far you go and however often you change; directions are named after end stations (Dirección Pantitlán); and every line has a number or letter and a colour. So the fare doesn't depend on distance, and signs don't use north or south.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this Mexican address.

image.alt: An envelope with an invented address: Sra. Laura Méndez Ruiz, Calle Fresno 27, Int. 4, Col. Las Palmas, C.P. 62050, Cuernavaca, Morelos. Six parts are numbered: Calle Fresno, 27, Int. 4, Col. Las Palmas, C.P. 62050 and Cuernavaca, Morelos.

questions.explanation: Calle Fresno is the street; 27 the building number (número exterior); Int. 4 the flat or office (número interior); Col. Las Palmas the colonia; C.P. 62050 the five-digit postcode; and Cuernavaca, Morelos the city and the state. The address has no alcaldía (that's only in Mexico City) and no country line.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Take line 2 towards Tasqueña. (to a stranger)
questions.explanation: The usted command tome, the line, then dirección + the end station: Tome la línea 2 dirección Tasqueña. Metro directions are named after end stations, not compass points.

questions.stem: A label says "una tableta cada 8 horas". What does it mean?
choices: one tablet after 8 hours of sleep
questions.explanation: Cada means every, each: every 8 hours, which is three times a day. "8 times a day" would be 8 veces al día.

questions.stem: Look at the label. How much syrup does it say a 9-year-old child takes?

image.alt: The label of the invented cough syrup TOSINA from the lesson. Dosis: Adultos: 10 ml cada 8 horas. Niños de 6 a 12 años: 5 ml cada 8 horas. Niños menores de 6 años: consulte a su médico. Agítese antes de usarse. No se deje al alcance de los niños. Consérvese en un lugar fresco y seco. Si los síntomas continúan, consulte a su médico.

questions.explanation: A 9-year-old is in the group niños de 6 a 12 años: 5 ml cada 8 horas. The 10 ml dose is for adults, and "consulte a su médico" is for children under 6 (menores de 6 años).

questions.stem: What does "No se deje al alcance de los niños" mean?
choices: Keep out of the reach of children.
Do not give to children at night.
questions.explanation: It's the standard sentence on Mexican medicines: keep out of the reach of children (literally "is not to be left within reach of children"). It's an impersonal se instruction.

questions.stem: A man tells the doctor he is allergic to penicillin. Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: Use the adjective with ser and a: Soy alérgico a la penicilina (a woman: alérgica). Or use the noun with tener: Tengo alergia a la penicilina. Alergia is a noun, so estoy / soy alergia is wrong.

questions.stem: At the pharmacy, the pharmacist asks: "¿Tiene receta?" What is she asking for?
questions.explanation: At the doctor's and the pharmacy, la receta is a prescription. In the kitchen the same word means a recipe. In Mexico antibiotics are sold only with a receta.

questions.stem: Which number do you call in an emergency anywhere in Mexico?
questions.explanation: 911 has been Mexico's national emergency number since January 2017 (it started in 16 states in October 2016), for police, fire and ambulance. It replaced several older numbers.

questions.stem: What is a "consultorio" next to a pharmacy in Mexico?
choices: A small doctor's office where a doctor sees patients, usually without an appointment
The emergency department of a hospital
A shop that sells only natural remedies
The office where you pay for health insurance
questions.explanation: Many Mexican pharmacies have a consultorio next door: a general doctor sees patients for a low fee (sometimes free) and can write a prescription. The hospital emergency department is Urgencias.

questions.stem: In Spain someone says "Estoy constipado". What do they mean?
choices: I have a cold (a blocked nose).
questions.explanation: Constipado is a false friend: in Spain it means having a cold. "Constipated" is estreñido. Dizzy is mareado and tired is cansado.

questions.stem: The pharmacist asks: "¿Desde cuándo tiene tos?" Which answer fits?
questions.explanation: ¿Desde cuándo? asks since when, so you answer with a time: Desde hace tres días (for three days). Cada ocho horas is how often to take a medicine, and me lo llevo means "I'll take it".

questions.stem: Write the missing word (a doctor's prescription): "Para este antibiótico necesita una ___."
questions.explanation: La receta is a prescription. In Mexico antibiotics have needed a prescription since 2010.

questions.stem: Match each sentence to its meaning.
questions.explanation: la tos = cough; me duele la garganta = my throat hurts; mareado = dizzy; el catarro = a cold; me siento mal = I feel ill. Allergic would be Tengo alergia, and a temperature Tengo fiebre.

questions.stem: Which of these label instructions use the impersonal se? Select all that apply.
choices: Consérvese en un lugar fresco y seco.
No se deje al alcance de los niños.
questions.explanation: Agítese, Consérvese and No se deje have se joined to or before the verb and speak to nobody in particular: "is to be shaken, kept, not left". Tome and Consulte are ordinary usted commands, addressed to you.

questions.stem: Put this short conversation at the pharmacy in order.
choices: Cliente: Tengo tos y me duele la garganta.
Farmacéutico: Tome este jarabe cada ocho horas.
questions.explanation: The pharmacist asks what's wrong, the customer gives the symptoms, the pharmacist asks since when, the customer answers, and only then does the pharmacist give instructions with an usted command.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I have a cough and a sore throat.
questions.explanation: Tengo tos (I have a cough) and me duele la garganta (my throat hurts), with the article la, not mi. The two halves can come in either order.

questions.stem: Complete with the preterite: "Anoche yo ___ el libro." (terminar)
questions.explanation: For yo, -ar verbs take -é in the preterite: "terminé". "Terminó" is the él/ella/usted form, "termino" is the present (I finish), and "terminí" uses the -er/-ir ending on an -ar verb.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "She spoke with the teacher"?
questions.explanation: The él/ella form of an -ar verb ends in -ó with an accent: "habló". Without the accent, "hablo" is "I speak" (present). "Hablé" is "I spoke", and "habla" is "she speaks".

questions.stem: What is the yo preterite of "llegar" (to arrive)?
questions.explanation: -gar verbs add a u before -é so the g keeps its hard sound: "llegué". "Llegé" would sound like "lle-HÉ". "Llegó" is the él form, which needs no change because g is before o.

questions.stem: Complete: "¿Qué ___ tú el sábado?" (hacer)
questions.explanation: "Hacer" has the strong stem hic- in the preterite: hice, hiciste, hizo. The tú form is "hiciste". "Hizo" is the él/usted form. "Haciste" uses the infinitive stem, which is wrong, and "hacías" is a different past tense (the imperfect) that this lesson doesn't use.

questions.stem: In "Fui al cine anoche", which verb is "fui"?
