glossary.definition: A word or phrase that tells you when something happens, and so which tense to use: ayer, anoche, el año pasado (preterite); hoy, ahora, todos los años (present); mañana, el próximo año (ir a + infinitive); alguna vez, nunca, ya (present perfect).

The present tense used to tell a story that happened in the past, to make it feel close and alive: Los dioses crean el mundo… (The gods create the world…). Common in retellings, summaries and jokes; the time is clear from the start of the story.
A word one language takes from another, usually adapting its sounds and spelling: English patio and rodeo come from Spanish; Spanish el fútbol and el suéter come from English.

Moving between two languages within one conversation or one sentence, as many bilingual people do: Mañana tengo un meeting, pero después vamos al cine. It follows patterns and is normal among bilinguals.

A word that looks like a word in another language but means something different: embarazada means pregnant (not embarrassed), la librería is a bookshop (not a library), el éxito is success (not an exit).

A sound made with the mouth open and the air flowing freely. Spanish has five vowel sounds, written a, e, i, o, u. They are short and pure, keep the same sound stressed or not, and are never silent except for the u in que, qui, gue, gui.

A unit of a word built around one vowel sound: ho-la has two syllables, te-lé-fo-no four. When i or u stands next to another vowel the two usually make one syllable (gra-cias, bue-nos) unless a written accent splits them (dí-a).

The syllable said a little louder and longer than the others. In Spanish, words ending in a vowel, n or s stress the second-to-last syllable (HO-la, GRA-cias); words ending in another consonant stress the last (fa-VOR). Exceptions carry a written accent.

The mark ´ over a vowel (á é í ó ú). It shows the stressed syllable when a word breaks the stress rule (adiós, lápiz, teléfono), tells apart pairs of words (sí/si), and marks question words (¿qué?). It is part of the spelling, also on capital letters.
A written accent that tells apart two words spelled the same, usually short ones: sí (yes) / si (if), tú (you) / tu (your), él (he) / el (the). Question words also carry one: qué, cómo, cuándo.

Pronouncing s, z, and c before e or i all as "s": cinco, zeta and sí all start with the same sound. It is the norm in all of Latin America; most of Spain says z and ce, ci like English "th" instead (distinción).

Pronouncing ll and y the same, like the y of English "yes": llamo and yo start with the same sound. It is the norm in almost the whole Spanish-speaking world; in Argentina and Uruguay the shared sound is "sh" or "zh" (sheísmo).

Speaking to someone with usted (or ustedes) instead of tú, to show respect or distance: with strangers, older people, at work, with officials. Usted takes the same verb forms as él and ella: usted es, usted habla.

The basic form of a verb, the one in the dictionary. Spanish infinitives end in -ar (hablar), -er (comer) or -ir (vivir); reflexive ones add -se (llamarse). After another verb the infinitive stays unchanged: necesito estudiar.

Changing a verb's ending to show who does the action (and when): hablar → hablo, hablas, habla, hablamos, hablan. Regular verbs follow the pattern of their family (-ar, -er, -ir); irregular verbs such as ser (soy, eres, es) must be learned.

A word that opens a question needing more than yes or no: quién (who), cómo (how), dónde (where), qué (what), cuándo (when), por qué (why), cuál (which), cuántos (how many). In questions it always has a written accent.

Dropping the end of a word in front of a noun. Uno becomes un (un año, veintiún años) and ciento becomes cien when it stands for exactly 100 (cien años). Later you will meet buen and mal before masculine nouns.

A word for the person doing the action: yo, tú, usted, él, ella, nosotros/nosotras, ustedes, ellos, ellas. Spanish usually leaves it out because the verb ending shows the person; it is used for contrast, emphasis or clarity.
The part of a verb left when you remove the infinitive ending: habl- from hablar, trabaj- from trabajar. The endings for each person are added to it: habl-o, habl-as.
The part added to a verb stem to show the person (and tense). Present -ar endings: -o, -as, -a, -amos, (-áis), -an. Because the ending shows who acts, the subject pronoun is usually dropped.
A verb whose forms all follow the pattern of its family, so they can be built from the stem: hablar → hablo, hablas, habla. Irregular verbs, such as ser, have forms that must be learned one by one.
The verb form for now and for habits: hablo can mean "I speak", "I am speaking" or "I do speak". It is also used for near plans and suggestions: Hoy trabajo hasta las cinco. ¿Estudiamos juntos?

A question answered with sí or no. In Spanish it uses the same words as a statement, with the voice rising at the end and ¿ … ? in writing: ¿Hablas español? The subject may also follow the verb: ¿Habla usted inglés?

A regular way of speaking a language in one region or community, with its own sounds, words and forms. Mexican, Caribbean, Río de la Plata, Andean and Spanish (Spain) Spanish are all correct varieties of one language.

Softening an s at the end of a syllable to a breathy h, or dropping it: ¿Cómo estás? sounds like "KOH-mo eh-TAH". Typical of the Caribbean and many coasts, and also heard in much of Central America, Chile, Argentina and southern Spain.

The pronunciation of central and northern Spain in which z, and c before e or i, sound like English "th" in "think", while s stays "s": casa (house) and caza (hunting) sound different. It is not a lisp. Latin America uses seseo instead.
Pronouncing ll and y like "sh" (or, in the older form, like the "zh" in "measure"): me llamo sounds like "meh SHAH-mo". Typical of Argentina and Uruguay.

Using vos instead of tú for informal "you", with its own verb forms: vos sos (tú eres), vos hablás (tú hablas). Standard in Argentina and common in Uruguay, Paraguay and much of Central America. This course teaches tú; learn vos for recognition.

A word placed before a name to show respect. Don and doña go before a first name (don Javier, doña Carmen); professional titles such as licenciado, ingeniero and doctora go before a surname or stand alone.
Addressing someone as tú instead of usted. Moving from usted to tú is usually offered by the older or more senior person: ¿Nos tuteamos? In Mexico also: Háblame de tú.
Using usted with people you are close to, such as friends, partners and children. Common in parts of Colombia (for example Bogotá and Antioquia), where it can sound warm rather than distant.

The group a Spanish noun belongs to: masculine or feminine. It is a property of the word, not of the thing, and it decides the form of articles and adjectives (el libro nuevo, la mesa nueva). Learn every noun with its article.
One of the two Spanish genders. Masculine nouns take el, un, los, unos: el libro, un mapa. Most nouns in -o are masculine, with exceptions such as la mano and la foto.

One of the two Spanish genders. Feminine nouns take la, una, las, unas: la mesa, una canción. Most nouns in -a, and all nouns in -ción and -dad, are feminine; el mapa, el día and el idioma are exceptions.
The word for "the": el (masculine singular), la (feminine singular), los (masculine plural, or a mixed group), las (feminine plural).
The word for "a" or "an": un (masculine), una (feminine). The plurals unos and unas mean "some" or "a few".

The form of a noun or adjective for more than one. Spanish adds -s after a vowel (libros), -es after a consonant (papeles), and changes z to c (lápices). Written accents can appear or vanish (canciones, jóvenes).
A word before a noun that says whose it is: mi(s), tu(s), su(s), nuestro/nuestra/nuestros/nuestras. It agrees with the thing owned, not with the owner: mis hermanos, nuestra casa.
An adjective that says where someone or something is from: mexicano, española, canadiense. Written with a small letter; it agrees like other adjectives (-o → -a; consonant + -a; -ense unchanged).
Matching gender and number: an adjective takes the gender and number of its noun (una mochila roja, unos libros nuevos). A masculine and a feminine noun together take a masculine plural adjective.

The language a country uses for government, courts and schools. Some countries name it in their constitution (de jure); in others, such as Mexico and Argentina, Spanish is official only in practice (de facto).

An ending that makes a word small or affectionate: -ito, -ita (perrito, abuelita), -cito after -e and many words in -n or -r (cafecito, amorcito). The noun keeps its gender (el mapita), and spelling changes keep the sound (chiquito, amiguito).
An affectionate way to speak to someone: mijo, mija, mi amor, mi vida, cariño. Some are used only within a family or between partners.

Words that say where something is in relation to something else: en (in, on), encima de (on top of), debajo de (under), al lado de (next to), enfrente de (in front of, opposite), detrás de (behind), entre (between). Most end in de, and de + el joins to del: al lado del sofá.

The small words me, te, le, nos, les that say to whom or for whom something happens. With gustar they show who likes something: Me gusta el café (coffee is pleasing to me). They go before the conjugated verb; add a mí, a ti, a él… for emphasis or clarity.

Words that point to something: este, esta, estos, estas (this, these, near me), ese, esa, esos, esas (that, those, near you) and aquel (that, over there). They agree with the noun: esta mochila, esos lentes. Esto and eso refer to something without naming it: ¿Qué es eso?

The form used to compare two things. Spanish puts más (more) or menos (less) before the adjective and que after it: más barato que (cheaper than). Equal things use tan … como (as … as). Bueno and malo have their own comparatives: mejor (better) and peor (worse).

A Spanish word borrowed from Nahuatl, the language of the Aztecs, which is still spoken in Mexico. Many are foods and plants: aguacate (from ahuacatl), elote (elotl), jitomate (xitomatl), tomate (tomatl), chile; also tianguis (tianquiztli, market).

The Spanish pattern for "chicken taco" or "orange juice": the main thing comes first and the second noun is joined with de. un taco de pollo, jugo de naranja, sopa de verduras. Quantities work the same way: un kilo de jitomates.

A way of asking for something that sounds friendly rather than bossy. In Mexican Spanish a present-tense question with usted is the usual polite request in shops and restaurants: ¿Me da un café? (Can I have a coffee?), ¿Me trae la cuenta? (Could you bring me the check?). Quisiera… (I would like…) is also polite.

The words lo, la, los, las meaning "it", "him", "her" or "them": the thing or person the verb acts on. They agree with the noun they replace and go before the conjugated verb: ¿Me lo deja en trescientos? (Will you let me have it for 300?), about el sombrero; ¿Me la deja…?, about la bolsa. Taught fully at A2.

The everyday way to talk about plans and the future: a present form of ir, then a, then a verb in the infinitive. Voy a ver una película (I'm going to see a film). Only ir changes; the infinitive never does.

A verb whose last stem vowel changes when it is stressed: e → ie (quiero), o → ue (puedo), u → ue (juego) or e → i (pido). In the present the change happens in yo, tú, él and ellos but not in nosotros (queremos), so the changed forms make a "boot" shape in the table. The endings stay regular.

A verb used with a pronoun that refers back to the subject, often for things you do to yourself: levantarse (to get up), bañarse (to shower). The dictionary form ends in -se; in a sentence the pronoun changes with the person: me levanto, te levantas, se levanta, nos levantamos, se levantan.

The pronouns me, te, se, nos, os and se used with reflexive verbs. They go before a conjugated verb (Me levanto), or on the end of an infinitive or an affirmative command (Voy a levantarme, ¡Levántate!).

A present-tense yo form that does not follow the regular pattern, while the other persons do: hago (hacer), salgo (salir), pongo (poner), sé (saber), conozco (conocer). Verbs that add a g in yo (hago, salgo, pongo, tengo, vengo) are often called yo-go verbs.

Telling the time with the hours numbered 0 to 23, as on timetables, opening hours and tickets: 18:30 h = las dieciocho treinta = las seis y media de la tarde. In conversation Spanish speakers usually switch to the 12-hour clock.

A phrase copied word for word from another language's structure. The Spanish Academy suggests that jugar fútbol (without al) is probably a calque of English "play football"; it is accepted as valid in Latin American Spanish.

The verb form for telling or asking someone to do something. The tú command is the él form of the present (toma, sigue), with eight short irregulars: di, haz, ve, pon, sal, sé, ten, ven. The usted command takes the yo form, drops -o and adds -e for -ar verbs or -a for -er and -ir verbs (tome, coma, siga, tenga), with spelling changes (cruce, llegue, busque) and five irregulars (sea, vaya, sepa, esté, dé). Ustedes adds -n (tomen). Negative commands use other forms (A2).

The little word a that Spanish puts before a direct object that is a specific person: Conozco a Ana. Espero a mi amiga. It has no English translation and is not used with places or things: Conozco Puebla. Espero el camión.

A number that gives a position in a series: primero (first), segundo (second), tercero (third). Primero and tercero shorten to primer and tercer before a masculine singular noun. In Latin American dates only the first day uses an ordinal: el primero de mayo, but el dos de mayo.
A verb used without any subject, not even "it": Llueve (it rains), Nieva (it snows). Weather expressions with hace work the same way: Hace frío. Spanish never adds a word for "it" here.

Se joined to a verb to give an instruction or a rule that addresses nobody in particular, common on labels and signs: Agítese antes de usarse (shake before use), Consérvese en un lugar fresco (store in a cool place), No se deje al alcance de los niños. At A1, recognize it; you don't need to produce it.

The Spanish past tense for finished events at a finished time: comí (I ate), fui (I went), Nací en 1995 (I was born in 1995). In Mexico and most of Latin America it is the everyday past, even for events earlier today.

A group of irregular preterites with a new stem and the endings -e, -iste, -o, -imos, -ieron, with no written accents: tener → tuve, tuvo; hacer → hice, hizo; poder → pude; venir → vine; estar → estuve.
The past form made with haber (he, has, ha, hemos, han) + a past participle: he comido (I have eaten). Used for experiences up to now and with ya / todavía no; in Spain also for events of today.
A helper verb that carries the person and tense while another verb carries the meaning. In the Spanish present perfect the auxiliary is haber: he, has, ha, hemos, han.

The verb form used after haber in the perfect: -ar → -ado (hablado), -er/-ir → -ido (comido, vivido). Irregular ones include hecho, dicho, visto, puesto, escrito, abierto, vuelto, roto. After haber it never changes.
A word that joins two ideas and shows how they relate: adding (y, además), contrasting (pero), giving a reason (porque) or a result (entonces).
In Spanish, when a negative word such as nada, nadie or nunca comes after the verb, no goes before the verb as well: No veo nada (I don't see anything). It is correct and required, not a mistake.
A past tense for background, descriptions and habits (era, estaba, había, hacía frío), beside the preterite, which tells the events. Taught at A2; this course shows it for recognition only.

references.title: Articles, gender, plurals and agreement
references.body:
## Articles

| | masculine | feminine |
|---|---|---|
| the (singular) | el | la |
| the (plural) | los | las |
| a, an | un | una |
| some | unos | unas |

- *a* + *el* = *al*, *de* + *el* = *del*: *Voy al parque. Vengo del mercado.* (No contraction with
  *la, los, las*, or with the pronoun *él*.)
- Feminine nouns that begin with a stressed *a-* or *ha-* take *el* and *un* in the singular, but
  stay feminine: *el agua fría, un hambre terrible*; plural *las aguas*.
- A mixed group takes the masculine plural: *los padres* (parents), *los niños* (children, boys
  and girls).

## Gender of nouns

| Usually masculine | Usually feminine |
|---|---|
| -o: *el libro, el carro* | -a: *la casa, la mesa* |
| -or: *el color, el doctor* | -ción, -sión: *la canción, la dirección* |
| -ma (from Greek): *el problema, el idioma* | -dad, -tad: *la ciudad, la universidad* |
| days, months, numbers, colours used as nouns | letters of the alphabet: *la eñe* |

Common exceptions to learn by heart: *el día, el mapa, el sofá* (masculine with -a); *la mano,
la foto* (feminine with -o; *foto* is short for *fotografía*). Nouns ending in -e or another consonant can be either: *el cine, la noche,
el lápiz, la pared*. Learn every noun with its article.

People: *el amigo / la amiga, el profesor / la profesora*; nouns in -ista and -ante/-ente
change only the article: *el estudiante / la estudiante, el turista / la turista*.

## Plurals

| Singular ends in | Plural | Example |
|---|---|---|
| a vowel | + s | *el libro → los libros, el café → los cafés* |
| a consonant | + es | *el reloj → los relojes, la ciudad → las ciudades* |
| -z | -ces | *el lápiz → los lápices, feliz → felices* |
| unstressed vowel + s | no change | *el lunes → los lunes, el paraguas → los paraguas* |

Written accents follow the stress rules, so they can appear or vanish: *la canción → las
canciones, el inglés → los ingleses, el joven → los jóvenes, el examen → los exámenes*.

## Adjective agreement

Adjectives agree with the noun in gender and number and usually come after it.

| Masculine singular ends in | m. sg. | f. sg. | m. pl. | f. pl. |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| -o | *nuevo* | *nueva* | *nuevos* | *nuevas* |
| -e | *grande* | *grande* | *grandes* | *grandes* |
| a consonant | *azul* | *azul* | *azules* | *azules* |
| -z | *feliz* | *feliz* | *felices* | *felices* |
| nationality + consonant | *español* | *española* | *españoles* | *españolas* |
| -or (describing) | *trabajador* | *trabajadora* | *trabajadores* | *trabajadoras* |

- Nationality adjectives in -ense don't change for gender: *canadiense, estadounidense*.
- Colours named after things (*café*, *rosa*) often don't change: *zapatos café*, *playeras
  rosa*.
- Before a masculine singular noun, *bueno → buen*, *malo → mal*, *primero → primer*: *un buen
  amigo, el primer día*. *Grande → gran* before any singular noun, and then means "great":
  *una gran ciudad* (a great city), *una ciudad grande* (a big city).
- A noun of each gender together: masculine plural adjective: *el libro y la mochila son
  nuevos*.

## Demonstratives

| | masculine | feminine | neuter (no noun) |
|---|---|---|---|
| this / these (here) | este / estos | esta / estas | esto |
| that / those (near you) | ese / esos | esa / esas | eso |
| that / those (over there) | aquel / aquellos | aquella / aquellas | aquello |

*¿Qué es esto?* — What's this? *Esta playera es más barata que esa.* — This T-shirt is cheaper
than that one. *Aquel* is for recognition at A1.

## Possessive adjectives

They agree with the thing owned, not the owner. Only *nuestro* (and Spain's *vuestro*) has a
feminine form.

| Owner | one thing | several things |
|---|---|---|
| yo | mi | mis |
| tú | tu | tus |
| él, ella, usted | su | sus |
| nosotros, nosotras | nuestro / nuestra | nuestros / nuestras |
| ellos, ellas, ustedes | su | sus |

*Mi hermana y mis primos. Nuestra casa. Su carro* can mean his, her, their or your (*usted* /
*ustedes*) car; to be clear, say *el carro de él, el carro de ustedes*. *Tu* (your) has no
accent; *tú* (you) has one.

references.title: Numbers, time and dates
references.body:
## 0–29

| | | | | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 cero | 6 seis | 12 doce | 18 dieciocho | 24 veinticuatro |
| 1 uno | 7 siete | 13 trece | 19 diecinueve | 25 veinticinco |
| 2 dos | 8 ocho | 14 catorce | 20 veinte | 26 veintiséis |
| 3 tres | 9 nueve | 15 quince | 21 veintiuno | 27 veintisiete |
| 4 cuatro | 10 diez | 16 dieciséis | 22 veintidós | 28 veintiocho |
| 5 cinco | 11 once | 17 diecisiete | 23 veintitrés | 29 veintinueve |

16–29 are one word. Accents: *dieciséis, veintidós, veintitrés, veintiséis*.

## 30–100

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| 30 treinta | 60 sesenta | 90 noventa |
| 40 cuarenta | 70 setenta | 100 cien |
| 50 cincuenta | 80 ochenta | |

From 31 on, tens and units are joined by *y*, as separate words: *treinta y uno, cuarenta y
cinco, noventa y nueve*.

## 100 and up

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| 100 cien | 400 cuatrocientos | 800 ochocientos |
| 101 ciento uno | 500 quinientos | 900 novecientos |
| 200 doscientos | 600 seiscientos | 1,000 mil |
| 300 trescientos | 700 setecientos | 1,000,000 un millón |

(Irregular hundreds: 500, 700, 900.)

- *Cien* alone or before a noun (*cien pesos*); *ciento* before another number (*ciento
  veinte*). Never *un cien* or *un mil*: *mil pesos, dos mil*.
- Hundreds agree with feminine nouns: *doscientas personas, quinientas tortillas*, but
  *quinientos pesos* (*peso* is masculine).
- *Millón* is a noun: *un millón de personas, dos millones de pesos*.
- *Uno* becomes *un* before a masculine noun and *una* before a feminine one: *veintiún años,
  treinta y una personas*.
- Mexico and much of Latin America write *1,500.50* (comma for thousands, point for decimals),
  like the US; Spain and some other countries write *1.500,50*.
- Phone numbers are read in pairs: 55 12 34 56 78 → *cincuenta y cinco, doce, treinta y cuatro,
  cincuenta y seis, setenta y ocho*.

## Telling the time

| Time | Spanish |
|---|---|
| 1:00 | Es la una. |
| 3:00 | Son las tres. |
| 3:05 | Son las tres y cinco. |
| 3:15 | Son las tres y cuarto. (or y quince) |
| 3:30 | Son las tres y media. (or y treinta) |
| 3:45 | Son las cuatro menos cuarto. / Un cuarto para las cuatro. / Quince para las cuatro. |
| 3:50 | Son las cuatro menos diez. / Diez para las cuatro. |
| 12:00 noon | Es mediodía. / Son las doce del día. |
| 12:00 midnight | Es medianoche. |

- *Es la una* (singular), *son las dos…* (plural).
- *¿Qué hora es?* — What time is it? *¿A qué hora…?* — At what time…? *A las ocho.* — At eight.
- *de la mañana* (morning), *de la tarde* (afternoon and early evening), *de la noche* (night). Without a clock time: *por la mañana, por la tarde, por la noche*.
- Timetables use the 24-hour clock: *18:30 = las dieciocho treinta*.
- *Para* (Latin America, often with *faltan*: *Faltan diez para las cuatro*) and *menos*
  (everywhere) both say "to" the hour.

## Days and months

Days and months are masculine and written without a capital letter.

| Days | | Months | | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| lunes | Monday | enero | mayo | septiembre |
| martes | Tuesday | febrero | junio | octubre |
| miércoles | Wednesday | marzo | julio | noviembre |
| jueves | Thursday | abril | agosto | diciembre |
| viernes | Friday | | | |
| sábado | Saturday | | | |
| domingo | Sunday | | | |

- *el lunes* = on Monday (one), *los lunes* = on Mondays (every): no *en*.
- Plural: *los lunes … los viernes* (no change), *los sábados, los domingos*.
- *Setiembre* is an accepted spelling, used in some countries.

## Dates

| Question / pattern | Example |
|---|---|
| ¿Qué fecha es hoy? | Hoy es el 5 de mayo. |
| the 1st | el primero de mayo (in Spain also el uno de mayo) |
| written | 5 de mayo de 2026, 5/5/2026 (day/month/year) |
| years | 2026 = dos mil veintiséis; 1990 = mil novecientos noventa |
| ¿Cuándo es tu cumpleaños? | Es el 12 de octubre. |
| in a month | en julio; in a year: en 2025 |

Seasons: *la primavera, el verano, el otoño, el invierno*: *en verano / en el verano*.

references.title: Talking about the past
references.body:
## Which past?

| | Preterite (*pretérito indefinido*) | Present perfect (*pretérito perfecto*) |
|---|---|---|
| Form | one word: *hablé* | *he, has, ha…* + participle: *he hablado* |
| Use | finished actions at a finished time | experiences up to now; *ya / todavía no* |
| Time words | *ayer, anoche, el sábado, la semana pasada, en 2020, hace dos años* | *alguna vez, nunca, ya, todavía no, hasta ahora* |
| Example | *Ayer comí en casa de mi abuela.* | *¿Has probado el mole? — Todavía no.* |

In Mexico and most of Latin America the preterite is the normal past, even for today: *Hoy
comí tacos.* In Spain the perfect is common for today and this week: *Hoy he comido tacos.*
Both are correct Spanish; this course uses the preterite for finished events.

## Preterite: regular endings

| | -ar: hablar | -er: comer | -ir: vivir |
|---|---|---|---|
| yo | hablé | comí | viví |
| tú | hablaste | comiste | viviste |
| él, ella, usted | habló | comió | vivió |
| nosotros | hablamos | comimos | vivimos |
| (vosotros) | (hablasteis) | (comisteis) | (vivisteis) |
| ellos, ustedes | hablaron | comieron | vivieron |

- The accents matter: *hablo* (I speak) vs *habló* (he spoke).
- *Nosotros* in -ar and -ir looks like the present (*hablamos, vivimos*); context tells you
  which.
- -ar and -er stem-changing verbs don't change in the preterite: *pensé, volví, entendí*.

### Spelling changes in the yo form

| Ending | yo | Others |
|---|---|---|
| -car → -qué | *buscar → busqué, tocar → toqué, practicar → practiqué, explicar → expliqué* | *buscaste, buscó…* |
| -gar → -gué | *llegar → llegué, pagar → pagué, jugar → jugué* | *llegaste, llegó…* |
| -zar → -cé | *empezar → empecé, cruzar → crucé, almorzar → almorcé* | *empezaste, empezó…* |

### i → y between vowels

*leer: leí, leíste, leyó, leímos, leyeron*; also *creer (creyó), oír (oyó)*.

### -ir stem changers: he/she and they only

| | pedir (e → i) | dormir (o → u) | preferir (e → i) |
|---|---|---|---|
| él, ella, usted | pidió | durmió | prefirió |
| ellos, ustedes | pidieron | durmieron | prefirieron |

Also *repetir (repitió), seguir (siguió), vestirse (se vistió), elegir (eligió)*. The other
persons are regular: *pedí, pediste, pedimos*.

## Preterite: irregular verbs

*Ser* and *ir* share one set of forms; context tells you which: *Fui al cine* (I went), *Fue
divertido* (it was fun).

| | ser / ir | dar | ver |
|---|---|---|---|
| yo | fui | di | vi |
| tú | fuiste | diste | viste |
| él, ella, usted | fue | dio | vio |
| nosotros | fuimos | dimos | vimos |
| ellos, ustedes | fueron | dieron | vieron |

No written accents on *fui, fue, di, dio, vi, vio*.

The "strong" group: an irregular stem and its own endings, with no accents: *-e, -iste, -o,
-imos, -isteis, -ieron*.

| Infinitive | Stem | yo | él | ellos |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| tener | tuv- | tuve | tuvo | tuvieron |
| estar | estuv- | estuve | estuvo | estuvieron |
| poder | pud- | pude | pudo | pudieron |
| poner | pus- | puse | puso | pusieron |
| saber | sup- | supe | supo | supieron |
| querer | quis- | quise | quiso | quisieron |
| venir | vin- | vine | vino | vinieron |
| hacer | hic- | hice | hizo | hicieron |
| decir | dij- | dije | dijo | dijeron |

*Hizo* is spelled with z to keep the sound; *decir* (and *traer*: *trajeron*) drop the i in
the *ellos* form.

## Present perfect

*Haber* (present) + past participle. The participle never changes.

| | haber | + participle |
|---|---|---|
| yo | he | hablado |
| tú | has | comido |
| él, ella, usted | ha | vivido |
| nosotros | hemos | estado |
| (vosotros) | (habéis) | |
| ellos, ustedes | han | ido |

### Participles

| Regular | | Irregular | |
|---|---|---|---|
| -ar → -ado | *hablar → hablado* | *hacer → hecho* | *decir → dicho* |
| -er, -ir → -ido | *comer → comido, vivir → vivido* | *ver → visto* | *poner → puesto* |
| accent after a, e, o | *leer → leído, oír → oído, creer → creído* | *escribir → escrito* | *abrir → abierto* |
| | | *volver → vuelto* | *romper → roto* |

- Nothing goes between *haber* and the participle; *no* and pronouns go before: *No he comido.
  ¿Te has levantado?*
- *Ser* and *ir* stay apart: *he sido* (I have been), *he ido* (I have gone).
- *Ya* (already, yet), *todavía no* (not yet), *nunca* (never), *alguna vez* (ever):
  *¿Ya has comido? — Sí, ya he comido. / No, todavía no.*

## Time words

| Preterite | Perfect |
|---|---|
| ayer — yesterday | hoy (in Spain) — today |
| anoche — last night | esta semana (in Spain) — this week |
| anteayer — the day before yesterday | alguna vez — ever |
| el lunes pasado, el año pasado — last Monday, last year | nunca — never |
| la semana pasada — last week | ya / todavía no — already / not yet |
| hace dos días — two days ago | hasta ahora — so far |
| en 2020 — in 2020 | |

references.title: The present tense, reflexive verbs and commands
references.body:
## Regular endings

Stem = infinitive minus *-ar, -er, -ir*. The *vosotros* forms (Spain) are in brackets: you'll
see them in books from Spain, but this course doesn't drill them.

| | -ar: hablar | -er: comer | -ir: vivir |
|---|---|---|---|
| yo | hablo | como | vivo |
| tú | hablas | comes | vives |
| él, ella, usted | habla | come | vive |
| nosotros, nosotras | hablamos | comemos | vivimos |
| (vosotros) | (habláis) | (coméis) | (vivís) |
| ellos, ellas, ustedes | hablan | comen | viven |

-er and -ir differ only in the *nosotros* (and *vosotros*) form. *Usted* takes the *él* form,
*ustedes* the *ellos* form.

## Stem-changing verbs

The stressed stem vowel changes in every form except *nosotros* (and *vosotros*): the four
changed forms make a "boot" shape in the table. The endings stay regular.

| | e → ie: querer | o → ue: poder | u → ue: jugar | e → i: pedir |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| yo | quiero | puedo | juego | pido |
| tú | quieres | puedes | juegas | pides |
| él, ella, usted | quiere | puede | juega | pide |
| nosotros | queremos | podemos | jugamos | pedimos |
| ellos, ustedes | quieren | pueden | juegan | piden |

- e → ie: *pensar, preferir, empezar, entender, cerrar, perder, despertarse, nevar (nieva)*.
- o → ue: *dormir, volver, almorzar, costar, encontrar, contar, probar, aprobar, acostarse,
  doler, llover (llueve)*.
- e → i (only -ir verbs): *pedir, repetir, seguir, vestirse, elegir*.

## Irregular yo forms

Only *yo* is irregular; the rest are regular (or stem-changing, as marked).

| Verb | yo | then |
|---|---|---|
| hacer | hago | haces, hace… |
| poner | pongo | pones, pone… |
| salir | salgo | sales, sale… |
| saber | sé | sabes, sabe… |
| conocer | conozco | conoces, conoce… |
| ver | veo | ves, ve… |
| dar | doy | das, da… |
| tener (e → ie) | tengo | tienes, tiene, tenemos, tienen |
| venir (e → ie) | vengo | vienes, viene, venimos, vienen |
| decir (e → i) | digo | dices, dice, decimos, dicen |
| seguir (e → i) | sigo | sigues, sigue, seguimos, siguen |
| elegir (e → i) | elijo | eliges, elige, elegimos, eligen |

## The four big irregulars

| | ser | estar | ir | tener |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| yo | soy | estoy | voy | tengo |
| tú | eres | estás | vas | tienes |
| él, ella, usted | es | está | va | tiene |
| nosotros | somos | estamos | vamos | tenemos |
| (vosotros) | (sois) | (estáis) | (vais) | (tenéis) |
| ellos, ustedes | son | están | van | tienen |

Also irregular: *oír* (oigo, oyes, oye, oímos, oyen).

## Verb + infinitive

| Pattern | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| ir a + inf. | going to (plans) | *Voy a viajar en julio.* — I'm going to travel in July. |
| tener que + inf. | have to | *Tengo que trabajar.* — I have to work. |
| hay que + inf. | one has to (general) | *Hay que llegar temprano.* — You have to arrive early. |
| querer + inf. | want to | *Quiero aprender español.* |
| poder + inf. | can, be able to | *¿Puedes venir?* |
| preferir + inf. | prefer to | *Prefiero caminar.* |
| me gusta + inf. | I like to | *Me gusta nadar.* |

## Reflexive verbs

The pronoun matches the subject: *me, te, se, nos, (os), se*.

| levantarse | |
|---|---|
| yo | me levanto |
| tú | te levantas |
| él, ella, usted | se levanta |
| nosotros | nos levantamos |
| (vosotros) | (os levantáis) |
| ellos, ustedes | se levantan |

- Before a conjugated verb: *Me levanto a las siete.*
- Attached to an infinitive (or before the whole verb group): *Voy a bañarme* = *Me voy a bañar.*
- Attached to an affirmative command: *¡Levántate!*
- Stem changes still apply: *me despierto, me acuesto, me visto.*

## Commands (affirmative imperative)

| | tú | usted | ustedes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rule | = *él* present | yo present: -o → -e (-ar) / -a (-er, -ir) | usted + n |
| hablar | habla | hable | hablen |
| comer | come | coma | coman |
| abrir | abre | abra | abran |
| volver | vuelve | vuelva | vuelvan |
| seguir | sigue | siga | sigan |
| tener | ten | tenga | tengan |
| hacer | haz | haga | hagan |

Irregular *tú* commands: *decir → di, hacer → haz, ir → ve, poner → pon, salir → sal, ser → sé,
tener → ten, venir → ven*.

Spelling changes in the *usted* form keep the sound: -car → -que (*buscar → busque*), -gar →
-gue (*llegar → llegue, pagar → pague*), -zar → -ce (*cruzar → cruce*).

Irregular *usted* commands: *ser → sea, ir → vaya, saber → sepa, estar → esté, dar → dé*.

Pronouns attach to affirmative commands, and an accent keeps the stress: *levántate,
levántese*. Negative commands (*no hables*) use another form and come at A2.

references.title: Pronouns
references.body:
## Subject pronouns

| | Singular | | Plural | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1st | yo | I | nosotros / nosotras | we (nosotras: all female) |
| 2nd, informal | tú | you | ustedes | you all |
| 2nd, formal | usted | you | ustedes | you all |
| 3rd | él / ella | he / she | ellos / ellas | they (ellas: all female) |

- In Latin America *ustedes* is the only plural "you", friendly or formal. Spain uses *vosotros /
  vosotras* for friends (recognition only in this course).
- *Usted* and *ustedes* take third-person verbs: *usted habla, ustedes hablan*. In writing they
  are often shortened to *Ud.* and *Uds.*
- Subject pronouns are usually left out, because the verb ending shows the person: *Hablo
  español.* Use them for contrast or emphasis: *Yo soy de México, y ella es de Perú.*
- "It" as a subject has no pronoun: *Es grande.* — It's big.

## Tú or usted?

| Usually tú | Usually usted |
|---|---|
| friends, family, children | strangers, older people |
| people your age in casual places | at work with clients, officials, doctors |
| when someone uses tú with you | when someone uses usted with you, or you aren't sure |

Habits vary by country and family; *usted* is never wrong with a stranger. Some Colombians use
*usted* even with close friends, and in Argentina and parts of Central America people use *vos*
instead of *tú* (recognition only).

## Reflexive pronouns

| yo | tú | él, ella, usted | nosotros | (vosotros) | ellos, ustedes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| me | te | se | nos | (os) | se |

*Me llamo Ana. ¿A qué hora te levantas? Se baña por la mañana.*

## Indirect object pronouns with gustar, encantar and doler

The thing liked (or that hurts) is the subject, so the verb is singular or plural to match it.

| (for emphasis) | pronoun | + one thing / infinitive | + several things |
|---|---|---|---|
| a mí | me | me gusta el café | me gustan los tacos |
| a ti | te | te gusta bailar | te gustan las películas |
| a él, a ella, a usted | le | le duele la cabeza | le duelen los pies |
| a nosotros | nos | nos encanta la playa | nos encantan los perros |
| (a vosotros) | (os) | | |
| a ellos, a ellas, a ustedes | les | les gusta el fútbol | les gustan los deportes |

- *A + name or noun* to say who: *A Carlos le gusta el béisbol.*
- Agreeing: *A mí también* (me too, after a yes) / *A mí tampoco* (me neither, after a no).
  Disagreeing: *A mí sí* / *A mí no*.

## After prepositions

| | after a, de, para, sin, en… | with con |
|---|---|---|
| yo | mí (accent) | conmigo |
| tú | ti (no accent) | contigo |
| others | él, ella, usted, nosotros, ellos, ellas, ustedes | con él, con ustedes… |

*Este regalo es para ti. ¿Vienes conmigo?* (*Entre* uses *yo* and *tú*: *entre tú y yo*.)

## Direct object pronouns (preview)

*lo* (him, it, you formal masculine), *la* (her, it, you formal feminine), *los*, *las*. At A1
you meet them in chunks: *¿La playera? La compro.* — The T-shirt? I'll buy it. They are taught
fully at A2.

references.title: Ser, estar and hay
references.body:
## Ser or estar?

Both mean "to be". A rough guide for A1: *ser* says what something *is*; *estar* says where it
is or how it is right now.

| Use | Verb | Example |
|---|---|---|
| name, identity | ser | *Soy Laura. Es mi hermano.* |
| origin, nationality | ser | *Somos de Guadalajara. Es mexicana.* |
| job | ser | *Mi papá es ingeniero.* |
| what someone or something is like | ser | *La casa es grande. Eres muy simpático.* |
| time, date, price total | ser | *Son las tres. Hoy es lunes. Son 200 pesos.* |
| where an event takes place | ser | *La fiesta es en mi casa.* |
| where a person or thing is | estar | *El baño está a la derecha. Estoy en la oficina.* |
| feelings, temporary states | estar | *Estoy cansada. ¿Estás enfermo?* |
| condition right now | estar | *La tienda está cerrada. El café está frío.* |
| *¿Cómo …?* | both | *¿Cómo es Ana?* (What's Ana like?) / *¿Cómo está Ana?* (How is Ana?) |

Some adjectives change meaning:

| | with ser | with estar |
|---|---|---|
| aburrido | boring | bored |
| listo | clever | ready |
| rico | rich | tasty (food) |
| feliz | a happy person (both are common) | happy right now |

*Feliz* is used with both verbs in everyday speech; *contento* goes with *estar*.

## Hay or está?

*Hay* (from *haber*) means "there is" or "there are". It has one form for singular and plural.

| | Use | Example |
|---|---|---|
| hay | something exists, with *un/una*, a number, *mucho*, or no article | *Hay un sofá en la sala. Hay dos baños. No hay leche.* |
| está / están | where a specific (known) thing is, with *el/la/mi…* or a name | *El sofá está en la sala. Mis llaves están en la mesa.* |

- Question with *hay*: *¿Hay una farmacia cerca?* — Is there a pharmacy nearby?
- Question with *está*: *¿Dónde está la farmacia?* — Where is the pharmacy?
- Never *hay el…*: *Hay un banco aquí* but *El banco está aquí*.
- *Hay que* + infinitive = one has to: *Hay que pagar en efectivo.*

## Prepositions of place (with estar)

| Spanish | English |
|---|---|
| en | in, on, at |
| encima de | on top of |
| debajo de | under |
| al lado de | next to |
| enfrente de | opposite, in front of |
| detrás de | behind |
| entre | between |
| cerca de | near |
| lejos de | far from |

*De* + *el* = *del*: *al lado del sofá, cerca del centro*.

Feminine la tía (aunt). Los tíos can mean uncles, or uncles and aunts.

vocab.example: Los martes estudio por la tarde.
vocab.exampleEn: On Tuesdays I study in the afternoon.
vocab.note: From noon until it gets dark (about 7 or 8 p.m.): las cuatro de la tarde.

vocab.example: Ceno a las nueve de la noche.
vocab.exampleEn: I have dinner at nine at night.

vocab.note: Masculine, although it ends in -a: el día, buenos días.

vocab.example: Trabajo cinco días a la semana.
vocab.exampleEn: I work five days a week.

vocab.example: ¿Qué planes tienes para el fin de semana?
vocab.exampleEn: What plans do you have for the weekend?

vocab.example: Los lunes tengo clase de español.
vocab.exampleEn: On Mondays I have Spanish class.
vocab.note: Lowercase. el lunes = on Monday, los lunes = on Mondays.

vocab.example: El martes trabajo hasta las seis.
vocab.exampleEn: On Tuesday I work until six.
On Wednesdays I go to the gym.

vocab.example: Los sábados como con mis abuelos.
vocab.exampleEn: On Saturdays I eat with my grandparents.

vocab.example: Siempre llego temprano a la oficina.
vocab.exampleEn: I always arrive at the office early.

vocab.example: A veces estudio por la noche.

vocab.note: Before the verb alone (Nunca trabajo), or after it with no (No trabajo nunca).

vocab.example: Mi papá siempre toma café a las siete.
vocab.exampleEn: My dad always has coffee at seven.
I listen to music every day.

vocab.example: La clase es a las nueve.
vocab.note: a + el = al: Voy al parque.
por la mañana / tarde / noche = in the morning / afternoon / at night (no clock time).
Clock time is la hora: ¿Qué hora es? Also the weather (lesson 19).

forms.present: voy, vas, va, vamos, vais, van
forms.preterite: fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fuisteis, fueron
forms.imperfect: iba, ibas, iba, íbamos, ibais, iban
forms.subjunctive: vaya, vayas, vaya, vayamos, vayáis, vayan

vocab.exampleEn: Where are you going? — I'm going to the cinema.
vocab.note: Irregular: voy, vas, va, vamos, van. ir a + infinitive = going to.

forms.present: vengo, vienes, viene, venimos, venís, vienen
forms.preterite: vine, viniste, vino, vinimos, vinisteis, vinieron
forms.subjunctive: venga, vengas, venga, vengamos, vengáis, vengan

vocab.exampleEn: Are you coming to my party on Saturday?
vocab.note: vengo, vienes, viene, venimos, vienen. Toward the speaker only; to go toward the listener use ir (¡Ya voy!).

vocab.exampleEn: Where are you going on Sunday?
We're going to the cinema tonight.

vocab.example: Mis padres van al teatro los viernes.
vocab.exampleEn: My parents go to the theatre on Fridays.

vocab.example: El museo está cerrado los lunes.
vocab.exampleEn: The museum is closed on Mondays.

vocab.example: Los domingos paseamos por el parque.
vocab.exampleEn: On Sundays we walk in the park.

vocab.example: Voy al gimnasio después del trabajo.
vocab.exampleEn: I go to the gym after work.

vocab.example: Hay un concierto en la plaza.
vocab.exampleEn: There's a concert in the square.

vocab.example: La fiesta es en mi casa.
vocab.exampleEn: The party is at my house.

vocab.example: Vamos a comer en un restaurante mexicano.
vocab.exampleEn: We're going to eat in a Mexican restaurant.
I'll wait for you in the café.

vocab.example: Vamos a ver el partido en mi casa.
vocab.exampleEn: We're going to watch the game at my house.
vocab.note: Also a political party.

vocab.exampleEn: Do you have plans for tonight?
Shall we go to the park? — What a good idea!
I'm inviting you to my party.
vocab.note: Te invito / Yo invito at a café can mean "it's on me".

vocab.example: El sábado voy a visitar el museo.
vocab.exampleEn: On Saturday I'm going to visit the museum.
vocab.note: With people add a: visitar a mis abuelos.

vocab.example: Los domingos paseamos por el centro.
vocab.exampleEn: On Sundays we go for a walk downtown.

forms.present: veo, ves, ve, vemos, veis, ven
forms.preterite: vi, viste, vio, vimos, visteis, vieron
forms.imperfect: veía, veías, veía, veíamos, veíais, veían
forms.subjunctive: vea, veas, vea, veamos, veáis, vean

vocab.example: Esta noche voy a ver una película.
vocab.exampleEn: Tonight I'm going to see a film.

vocab.example: Esta noche hay un concierto en el parque.
vocab.exampleEn: Tonight there's a concert in the park.

vocab.example: El próximo sábado vamos a la playa.
vocab.exampleEn: Next Saturday we're going to the beach.
vocab.note: la próxima semana = next week.

vocab.exampleEn: Shall we go to the cinema together?
vocab.note: Agrees: juntas for an all-female group.

vocab.exampleEn: Are you coming alone or with your sister?
vocab.note: Feminine sola. As an adverb solo also means "only": Solo tengo una hora.

vocab.exampleEn: Do you want to come? — Of course!

vocab.example: La gente va al parque los domingos.
vocab.exampleEn: People go to the park on Sundays.
vocab.note: Singular in Spanish, so the verb is singular: la gente es simpática.

forms.present: puedo, puedes, puede, podemos, podéis, pueden
forms.preterite: pude, pudiste, pudo, pudimos, pudisteis, pudieron
forms.subjunctive: pueda, puedas, pueda, podamos, podáis, puedan

vocab.note: o → ue: puedo, puedes, puede, podemos, pueden. + infinitive without a: Puedo nadar.

forms.present: juego, juegas, juega, jugamos, jugáis, juegan
forms.preterite: jugué, jugaste, jugó, jugamos, jugasteis, jugaron
forms.subjunctive: juegue, juegues, juegue, juguemos, juguéis, jueguen

vocab.note: u → ue: juego, juegas, jugamos. jugar fútbol or jugar al fútbol; instruments take tocar.

forms.present: prefiero, prefieres, prefiere, preferimos, preferís, prefieren
forms.preterite: preferí, preferiste, prefirió, preferimos, preferisteis, prefirieron
forms.subjunctive: prefiera, prefieras, prefiera, prefiramos, prefiráis, prefieran

vocab.note: e → ie: prefiero, prefieres, preferimos. Preterite prefirió, prefirieron.

forms.present: pienso, piensas, piensa, pensamos, pensáis, piensan
forms.subjunctive: piense, pienses, piense, pensemos, penséis, piensen

vocab.note: e → ie: pienso, piensas, pensamos. pensar en = to think about.

forms.present: empiezo, empiezas, empieza, empezamos, empezáis, empiezan
forms.preterite: empecé, empezaste, empezó, empezamos, empezasteis, empezaron
forms.subjunctive: empiece, empieces, empiece, empecemos, empecéis, empiecen

vocab.example: La clase empieza a las ocho.
vocab.note: e → ie: empiezo, empiezas, empezamos. empezar a + infinitive. Preterite empecé.

forms.present: entiendo, entiendes, entiende, entendemos, entendéis, entienden
forms.subjunctive: entienda, entiendas, entienda, entendamos, entendáis, entiendan

vocab.note: e → ie: entiendo, entiendes, entendemos.

forms.present: pierdo, pierdes, pierde, perdemos, perdéis, pierden
forms.subjunctive: pierda, pierdas, pierda, perdamos, perdáis, pierdan

vocab.note: e → ie: pierdo, pierdes, perdemos.

forms.present: duermo, duermes, duerme, dormimos, dormís, duermen
forms.preterite: dormí, dormiste, durmió, dormimos, dormisteis, durmieron
forms.subjunctive: duerma, duermas, duerma, durmamos, durmáis, duerman

vocab.example: Los domingos duermo hasta las nueve.
vocab.exampleEn: On Sundays I sleep until nine.
vocab.note: o → ue: duermo, duermes, dormimos. Preterite durmió, durmieron.

forms.present: vuelvo, vuelves, vuelve, volvemos, volvéis, vuelven
forms.subjunctive: vuelva, vuelvas, vuelva, volvamos, volváis, vuelvan

vocab.example: Vuelvo a casa a las seis.
vocab.exampleEn: I come back home at six.
vocab.note: o → ue: vuelvo, vuelves, volvemos. Participle vuelto.

forms.present: almuerzo, almuerzas, almuerza, almorzamos, almorzáis, almuerzan
forms.preterite: almorcé, almorzaste, almorzó, almorzamos, almorzasteis, almorzaron
forms.subjunctive: almuerce, almuerces, almuerce, almorcemos, almorcéis, almuercen

vocab.exampleEn: Shall we have lunch together on Saturday?
vocab.note: o → ue: almuerzo, almorzamos. In Mexico el almuerzo is often a late, hearty breakfast; the main meal is la comida.

forms.present: pido, pides, pide, pedimos, pedís, piden
forms.preterite: pedí, pediste, pidió, pedimos, pedisteis, pidieron
forms.subjunctive: pida, pidas, pida, pidamos, pidáis, pidan

vocab.note: e → i: pido, pides, pedimos. To ask a question is preguntar.

forms.present: repito, repites, repite, repetimos, repetís, repiten
forms.preterite: repetí, repetiste, repitió, repetimos, repetisteis, repitieron
forms.subjunctive: repita, repitas, repita, repitamos, repitáis, repitan

vocab.note: e → i: repito, repites, repetimos.

forms.present: cierro, cierras, cierra, cerramos, cerráis, cierran
forms.subjunctive: cierre, cierres, cierre, cerremos, cerréis, cierren

vocab.example: La tienda cierra a las ocho.
vocab.note: e → ie: cierro, cierras, cerramos.

vocab.example: Mi hermano juega fútbol con sus amigos.
vocab.exampleEn: My brother plays football with his friends.
vocab.note: In Mexico usually futbol, stressed on the last syllable (fut-BOL); both spellings are correct.

vocab.exampleEn: In Monterrey there's a lot of baseball.
vocab.note: In Mexico usually beisbol, stressed on the last syllable; both spellings are correct.
Mexico also basquetbol (stressed on the end); Spain el baloncesto.

vocab.example: Mi abuela nada todos los días.
Corro en el parque por la mañana.
vocab.exampleEn: I run in the park in the morning.

forms.preterite: toqué, tocaste, tocó, tocamos, tocasteis, tocaron

vocab.note: Instruments take tocar, sports take jugar. Preterite toqué.

vocab.example: Quiero aprender a tocar la guitarra.
vocab.exampleEn: I want to learn to play the guitar.
What do you do in your free time?

vocab.example: Mis hijos juegan videojuegos los sábados.
vocab.exampleEn: My children play video games on Saturdays.
I ride my bike on Sundays.
vocab.note: Mexico andar en bicicleta, Spain montar en bicicleta.

vocab.example: Me levanto a las seis y media.
vocab.exampleEn: I get up at half past six.
vocab.note: Reflexive: me levanto, te levantas, se levanta.

forms.present: me despierto, te despiertas, se despierta, nos despertamos, os despertáis, se despiertan
forms.subjunctive: me despierte, te despiertes, se despierte, nos despertemos, os despertéis, se despierten

vocab.note: e → ie: me despierto, te despiertas, nos despertamos.

forms.present: me acuesto, te acuestas, se acuesta, nos acostamos, os acostáis, se acuestan
forms.subjunctive: me acueste, te acuestes, se acueste, nos acostemos, os acostéis, se acuesten

vocab.exampleEn: We go to bed at eleven.
vocab.note: o → ue: me acuesto, te acuestas, nos acostamos.

vocab.example: ¿Te bañas por la mañana o por la noche?
vocab.exampleEn: Do you shower in the morning or at night?
vocab.note: In Mexico usually "to shower"; Spain ducharse.

vocab.example: Me lavo los dientes después de comer.
vocab.exampleEn: I brush my teeth after eating.
vocab.note: Body parts take the article: me lavo las manos, los dientes.

forms.present: me visto, te vistes, se viste, nos vestimos, os vestís, se visten
forms.preterite: me vestí, te vestiste, se vistió, nos vestimos, os vestisteis, se vistieron
forms.subjunctive: me vista, te vistas, se vista, nos vistamos, os vistáis, se vistan

vocab.exampleEn: My son gets dressed by himself.
vocab.note: e → i: me visto, te vistes, nos vestimos. Preterite se vistió.

forms.present: me voy, te vas, se va, nos vamos, os vais, se van
forms.imperfect: me iba, te ibas, se iba, nos íbamos, os ibais, se iban
forms.preterite: me fui, te fuiste, se fue, nos fuimos, os fuisteis, se fueron
forms.subjunctive: me vaya, te vayas, se vaya, nos vayamos, os vayáis, se vayan

vocab.note: ir with the reflexive pronoun: me voy, te vas, se va.

forms.present: hago, haces, hace, hacemos, hacéis, hacen
forms.preterite: hice, hiciste, hizo, hicimos, hicisteis, hicieron
forms.subjunctive: haga, hagas, haga, hagamos, hagáis, hagan

vocab.exampleEn: What are you doing on Saturday?
vocab.note: Irregular yo: hago. Preterite hice, hizo; participle hecho; tú command haz.

forms.present: salgo, sales, sale, salimos, salís, salen
forms.preterite: salí, saliste, salió, salimos, salisteis, salieron
forms.subjunctive: salga, salgas, salga, salgamos, salgáis, salgan

vocab.example: Salgo de casa a las siete.
vocab.note: Irregular yo: salgo. salir de = to leave a place; tú command sal.

forms.present: pongo, pones, pone, ponemos, ponéis, ponen
forms.preterite: puse, pusiste, puso, pusimos, pusisteis, pusieron
forms.subjunctive: ponga, pongas, ponga, pongamos, pongáis, pongan

vocab.example: Pongo las llaves en la mesa.
vocab.exampleEn: I put the keys on the table.
vocab.note: Irregular yo: pongo. Preterite puse; participle puesto; tú command pon. poner la mesa = to set the table.

forms.present: sé, sabes, sabe, sabemos, sabéis, saben
forms.preterite: supe, supiste, supo, supimos, supisteis, supieron
forms.subjunctive: sepa, sepas, sepa, sepamos, sepáis, sepan

vocab.example: No sé dónde está el museo.
vocab.exampleEn: I don't know where the museum is.
vocab.note: Irregular yo: sé (with an accent). saber + infinitive = know how to: Sé nadar. People and places: conocer.

vocab.exampleEn: On Saturdays I clean the house.
vocab.note: Regular: limpio, limpias (stress on LIM).

vocab.example: Yo lavo los platos y tú cocinas.
vocab.exampleEn: I wash the dishes and you cook.
vocab.note: lavar la ropa = to do the laundry. Washing yourself: lavarse.

vocab.example: Barro la cocina después de comer.
vocab.exampleEn: I sweep the kitchen after eating.

vocab.example: Pongo la ropa en la silla.
vocab.exampleEn: I put the clothes on the chair.
vocab.note: Singular in Spanish: la ropa está limpia.

vocab.example: Me lavo los dientes tres veces al día.
vocab.exampleEn: I brush my teeth three times a day.

vocab.note: Mexico la regadera; Spain and elsewhere la ducha.

vocab.example: Primero me baño y luego desayuno.
vocab.exampleEn: First I shower and then I have breakfast.
Afterwards we're going to the park.

vocab.example: Más tarde ceno con mi hermana.
vocab.exampleEn: Later I have dinner with my sister.

vocab.example: Finalmente me acuesto a las once.
vocab.exampleEn: Finally I go to bed at eleven.

vocab.note: + infinitive: antes de salir, antes de acostarme.

vocab.example: Después de comer, me lavo los dientes.
vocab.exampleEn: After eating, I brush my teeth.
vocab.note: + infinitive: después de trabajar, después de bañarme.

vocab.example: Mi rutina empieza a las seis.

vocab.exampleEn: What time do you get up?
vocab.note: Followed by a verb: ¿A qué hora empieza la clase? Answer with a las…

meanings: right now or in a little while (Mexico)
vocab.note: Mexico and much of Latin America: now, soon, a moment ago, or later. Context and tone decide.

vocab.exampleEn: I'll call you in a while.
vocab.note: Very common in Mexico: ¡Nos vemos al rato! = See you later!

vocab.exampleEn: I'll help you in a moment.
What are the museum's opening hours?

vocab.example: Abrimos desde las ocho hasta las diez.
vocab.exampleEn: We're open from eight until ten.
vocab.note: desde … hasta (from … until); everyday de … a.

vocab.example: El camión pasa cada quince minutos.
vocab.exampleEn: The bus comes every fifteen minutes.
vocab.note: Never changes: cada día, cada semana, cada dos horas.
Same form for masculine and feminine; plural puntuales.

vocab.example: La reunión empieza a las nueve en punto.
vocab.exampleEn: The meeting starts at nine sharp.

vocab.example: En hora pico el metro va lleno.
vocab.exampleEn: At rush hour the metro is full.
vocab.note: Mexico la hora pico; Spain la hora punta.

vocab.example: Su tarjeta llega en cinco días hábiles.
vocab.exampleEn: Your card arrives within five working days.
vocab.note: Monday to Friday, except public holidays. Common in official notices.

vocab.example: Mi equipo es el mejor de la liga.
vocab.exampleEn: My team is the best in the league.

vocab.note: meter un gol = to score a goal.

vocab.example: Los aficionados cantan en el estadio.
vocab.exampleEn: The fans sing in the stadium.
vocab.note: la aficionada for a woman.

vocab.example: El jugador número 9 mete un gol.
vocab.note: la jugadora for a woman.

vocab.exampleEn: A home run in the ninth inning!

vocab.example: Diego toca la trompeta en un mariachi.
vocab.exampleEn: Diego plays the trumpet in a mariachi band.
A mariachi band has several violins.

vocab.example: Ana toca el tambor, pero muy mal.
vocab.exampleEn: Ana plays the drum, but very badly.

vocab.example: Me gusta el ritmo de la cumbia.
vocab.exampleEn: I like the rhythm of cumbia.

vocab.example: Mi primo es el cantante del grupo.
vocab.exampleEn: My cousin is the band's singer.
vocab.note: Same form for a woman: la cantante.

vocab.example: Mi casa está en la calle Hidalgo.
vocab.exampleEn: My house is on Hidalgo Street.

vocab.note: Often written Av. on signs and in addresses.
vocab.example: El hotel está en la Avenida Juárez.
vocab.exampleEn: The hotel is on Juárez Avenue.

vocab.note: In Mexico the main square of a town is often called el zócalo; la plaza comercial is a shopping mall.
vocab.example: Hay una iglesia muy bonita en la plaza.
vocab.exampleEn: There's a very pretty church on the square.

vocab.example: La farmacia está en la esquina.
vocab.exampleEn: The pharmacy is on the corner.

vocab.note: Spain: la manzana (in everyday Mexican speech "apple", though Mexican maps and some addresses also use it for a block).
vocab.example: El banco está a dos cuadras.
vocab.exampleEn: The bank is two blocks away.

vocab.note: Also "bench" (a seat in a park).
vocab.exampleEn: Is there a bank near here?

vocab.example: La farmacia está abierta hasta las diez.
vocab.exampleEn: The pharmacy is open until ten.

vocab.example: El hospital está lejos del centro.
vocab.exampleEn: The hospital is far from downtown.

vocab.example: Mi oficina está en un edificio alto.
vocab.exampleEn: My office is in a tall building.

vocab.example: Cruce el puente y doble a la derecha.
vocab.exampleEn: Cross the bridge and turn right.

vocab.note: Also "metre" (a measure), with the same plural.
vocab.example: Tomo el metro para ir al trabajo.
vocab.exampleEn: I take the metro to go to work.

vocab.example: En el semáforo, doble a la izquierda.
vocab.exampleEn: At the traffic light, turn left.

vocab.note: la parada del camión / del autobús = the bus stop.
vocab.example: La parada está enfrente del banco.
vocab.exampleEn: The stop is opposite the bank.

vocab.note: Also "ticket" for a show in some countries (in Mexico usually el boleto).
vocab.example: La entrada del museo está en la plaza.
vocab.exampleEn: The museum's entrance is on the square.

vocab.example: El hotel está a la derecha.
vocab.exampleEn: The hotel is on the right.

vocab.example: Doble a la izquierda en la esquina.

vocab.note: Spain: todo recto. Don't mix it up with a la derecha (to the right).

forms.present: sigo, sigues, sigue, seguimos, seguís, siguen
forms.preterite: seguí, seguiste, siguió, seguimos, seguisteis, siguieron
forms.subjunctive: siga, sigas, siga, sigamos, sigáis, sigan

vocab.note: e → i and gu → g before o: sigo, sigues. Commands: sigue (tú), siga (usted).
vocab.example: Siga por esta calle hasta el puente.
vocab.exampleEn: Keep going along this street as far as the bridge.

vocab.note: Also common in Mexico: dar vuelta (Dé vuelta a la derecha). Spain usually says girar.
vocab.example: Doble a la derecha en el semáforo.
vocab.exampleEn: Turn right at the traffic light.

forms.preterite: crucé, cruzaste, cruzó, cruzamos, cruzasteis, cruzaron

vocab.note: z → c before e: crucé, and the usted command cruce.
vocab.example: Cruce la avenida en el semáforo.
vocab.exampleEn: Cross the avenue at the traffic light.

vocab.note: ¡Pase! = Come in! ¿Qué pasa? = What's happening? / What's wrong?
vocab.example: Pase por la plaza y siga derecho.
vocab.exampleEn: Go through the square and keep going straight ahead.

vocab.note: With estar: Estoy perdida (a woman speaking).
vocab.example: Disculpe, estoy perdido. ¿Dónde está el metro?
vocab.exampleEn: Excuse me, I'm lost. Where is the metro?

vocab.note: a + el = al: ¿Cómo llego al hospital?
vocab.exampleEn: Excuse me, how do I get to the square?

meanings: excuse me! (to get a stranger's attention)
vocab.note: The usted command of oír (to hear). Soften it: Oiga, disculpe…
vocab.exampleEn: Excuse me, sorry, where's the stop?

vocab.note: The usted command of mirar; the tú form is mira.
vocab.example: Mire, el banco está allá, en la esquina.
vocab.exampleEn: Look, the bank is over there, on the corner.

vocab.note: ¡Buen viaje! = Have a good trip!
vocab.example: El viaje a Oaxaca es largo.
vocab.exampleEn: The trip to Oaxaca is long.

vocab.note: Always plural: ir de vacaciones, estar de vacaciones.
vocab.example: En las vacaciones vamos a la playa.
vocab.exampleEn: On vacation we're going to the beach.
I'm going to Cancún by plane.

vocab.example: El aeropuerto está cerca de la ciudad.
vocab.exampleEn: The airport is near the city.

vocab.note: In Mexico usually el camión (for a city bus and a long-distance bus); el autobús is understood everywhere. A truck is also el camión.
vocab.example: El autobús para Puebla sale a las nueve.
vocab.exampleEn: The bus to Puebla leaves at nine.

vocab.note: Also "season" (las cuatro estaciones, lesson 19).
vocab.example: La estación del metro está a una cuadra.
vocab.exampleEn: The metro station is a block away.

vocab.example: El tren llega a las tres y media.
vocab.exampleEn: The train arrives at half past three.

vocab.note: Mexico and much of Latin America: el carro (also el coche in Mexico); Argentina and Chile: el auto; Spain: el coche.
vocab.example: No tengo carro; viajo en autobús.
vocab.exampleEn: I don't have a car; I travel by bus.
We take a taxi to the hotel.

vocab.note: Spain: el billete (which in Mexico is a banknote).
vocab.example: Un boleto para Guadalajara, por favor.

vocab.exampleEn: I need my passport to travel.

vocab.example: Mi maleta es azul y muy grande.
vocab.exampleEn: My suitcase is blue and very big.

vocab.example: El hotel está enfrente de la playa.
vocab.exampleEn: The hotel is opposite the beach.

vocab.note: A room in a house is usually el cuarto (lesson 10).
vocab.example: Quisiera una habitación para dos personas.
vocab.exampleEn: I'd like a room for two people.
I want to book a room.

vocab.note: subir al camión = to get on the bus; subir la escalera = to go up the stairs.
vocab.example: Subimos al tren en la estación central.
vocab.exampleEn: We get on the train at the central station.

vocab.note: Often bajarse: Me bajo en la próxima parada (I'm getting off at the next stop).
vocab.example: Bajamos del avión a las seis.
vocab.exampleEn: We get off the plane at six.

vocab.note: Spain: conducir.
No word for "for": Espero el autobús = I'm waiting for the bus.
vocab.example: Esperamos el camión en la parada.
vocab.exampleEn: We wait for the bus at the stop.

forms.present: conozco, conoces, conoce, conocemos, conocéis, conocen
forms.subjunctive: conozca, conozcas, conozca, conozcamos, conozcáis, conozcan

vocab.note: Irregular yo: conozco. Personal a before people: Conozco a Ana.
vocab.exampleEn: Have you been to Guadalajara? (literally: Do you know Guadalajara?)

vocab.example: La playa está a diez minutos del hotel.
vocab.exampleEn: The beach is ten minutes from the hotel.

vocab.note: Usually masculine; la mar appears in poetry and in sailors' speech.
vocab.example: El mar está muy tranquilo hoy.
vocab.exampleEn: The sea is very calm today.

vocab.example: Me gusta caminar en la montaña.
vocab.exampleEn: I like walking in the mountains.

vocab.example: El pueblo está al lado de un río.
vocab.exampleEn: The village is next to a river.

vocab.note: Also "a people" (el pueblo mexicano). A Pueblo Mágico is a Mexican town with that official tourism title.
vocab.example: Mis abuelos viven en un pueblo pequeño.
vocab.exampleEn: My grandparents live in a small town.

vocab.note: The opposite of la salida (departure). Airport signs: Llegadas, Salidas.
vocab.example: La llegada del tren es a las cinco.
vocab.exampleEn: The train's arrival is at five.

vocab.note: A one-way ticket is un boleto sencillo (Mexico) or de ida. Mexico also says viaje redondo for a round trip.
vocab.example: Un boleto de ida y vuelta, por favor.

vocab.note: The same word for a woman: la turista.
vocab.example: Hay muchos turistas en la plaza.
vocab.exampleEn: There are lots of tourists on the square.

vocab.note: el camión para Puebla = the bus to Puebla; para + infinitive = in order to.
vocab.example: Estudio español para viajar a México.
vocab.exampleEn: I'm studying Spanish to travel to Mexico.

vocab.note: masculine; used without an article and written without a capital: en enero.
vocab.example: En enero hace frío en el norte de México.
vocab.exampleEn: In January it's cold in the north of Mexico.

vocab.note: masculine; used without an article: en febrero.
masculine; used without an article: en marzo.
masculine; used without an article: en abril.
vocab.example: En abril hace mucho calor en Monterrey.
vocab.exampleEn: In April it's very hot in Monterrey.

vocab.note: masculine; used without an article: el 10 de mayo.
vocab.example: El Día de las Madres en México es el 10 de mayo.
vocab.exampleEn: Mother's Day in Mexico is on 10 May.

vocab.note: masculine; used without an article: en junio.
masculine; used without an article: en julio.
vocab.example: Vamos a la playa en julio.
vocab.exampleEn: We're going to the beach in July.

vocab.note: masculine; used without an article: en agosto.
vocab.example: En agosto llueve mucho en la Ciudad de México.
vocab.exampleEn: In August it rains a lot in Mexico City.

vocab.note: masculine; used without an article: el 16 de septiembre. Setiembre is also correct.
vocab.example: El 16 de septiembre es un día de fiesta en México.
vocab.exampleEn: 16 September is a holiday in Mexico.

vocab.note: masculine; used without an article: en octubre.
vocab.example: En octubre ya no llueve tanto.
vocab.exampleEn: In October it doesn't rain so much any more.

vocab.note: masculine; used without an article: el 2 de noviembre.
vocab.example: El 2 de noviembre es el Día de Muertos.
vocab.exampleEn: 2 November is the Day of the Dead.

vocab.note: masculine; used without an article: en diciembre.
vocab.example: En diciembre visito a mi familia.
vocab.exampleEn: In December I visit my family.

vocab.example: En la primavera hace buen tiempo.
vocab.exampleEn: In spring the weather is nice.

vocab.example: En el verano llueve mucho en el centro de México.
vocab.exampleEn: In summer it rains a lot in central Mexico.

vocab.example: En el invierno nieva en las montañas.
vocab.exampleEn: In winter it snows in the mountains.

vocab.note: A romantic date is la cita (lesson 20 uses it for an appointment).

vocab.example: Voy a México el próximo mes.
vocab.exampleEn: I'm going to Mexico next month.

vocab.note: The same form in the plural.
Before a masculine singular noun: primer (el primer día). In dates: el primero de mayo (Spain also el uno de mayo).
vocab.example: Hoy es el primero de junio.
vocab.exampleEn: Today is the first of June.

vocab.note: Masculine although it ends in -a. In Mexico el clima is everyday for "the weather"; el tiempo also means weather.
vocab.example: El clima de Cuernavaca es muy agradable.
vocab.exampleEn: The climate in Cuernavaca is very pleasant.

vocab.note: hace calor = it's hot (weather); tengo calor = I'm hot (a person).
hace frío = it's cold (weather); tengo frío = I'm cold (a person).
hace sol = it's sunny. The Peruvian currency is also el sol.
vocab.example: Hace sol y no hace viento.
vocab.exampleEn: It's sunny and there's no wind.

vocab.note: la temporada de lluvias = the rainy season.
vocab.example: Me gusta el sonido de la lluvia.
vocab.exampleEn: I like the sound of the rain.

vocab.note: o → ue. Used only in the third person: llueve (it rains, it's raining); past llovió. Not in the verb drills. Llueve mucho en agosto.
vocab.example: En la Ciudad de México llueve casi todas las tardes en julio.
vocab.exampleEn: In Mexico City it rains almost every afternoon in July.

vocab.note: e → ie. Used only in the third person: nieva (it snows, it's snowing); past nevó. Not in the verb drills.
vocab.exampleEn: It almost never snows in Monterrey.

vocab.note: hace viento = it's windy.
vocab.example: Hoy hace mucho viento en la playa.
vocab.exampleEn: It's very windy on the beach today.

vocab.note: With estar: Está nublado (it's cloudy).
vocab.example: El cielo está nublado; va a llover.
vocab.exampleEn: The sky is cloudy; it's going to rain.

vocab.note: ¡Ojo! on its own means "Watch out! / Careful!"
vocab.example: Mi hija tiene los ojos verdes.

vocab.note: The outer ear. Earache is usually dolor de oído (el oído = inner ear, hearing).
vocab.example: El perro tiene las orejas grandes.
Tengo la nariz roja por el frío.
vocab.exampleEn: My nose is red from the cold.

vocab.note: feminine although it ends in -o: la mano derecha.
vocab.example: Lávate las manos antes de comer.
vocab.exampleEn: Wash your hands before you eat.

vocab.note: Also common: la panza (informal), el abdomen (formal).

vocab.example: Me duele la espalda por la mochila.
vocab.exampleEn: My back hurts because of the backpack.

vocab.example: Después de correr me duelen las piernas.

vocab.note: a pie = on foot.
Works like gustar, so in practice only the third person: me duele la cabeza (one thing), me duelen los pies (several); past dolió, dolieron. o → ue. Not in the verb drills.
tener dolor de cabeza / de estómago = to have a headache / a stomach ache.
tener fiebre = to have a temperature.
Mexico and Colombia: la gripa; Spain and most other countries: la gripe. In Mexico tener gripa also covers a bad cold.
vocab.example: Tengo gripa y me quedo en casa.
vocab.exampleEn: I have the flu and I'm staying at home.

vocab.example: Tome una pastilla después de comer.

vocab.note: Also el medicamento (more formal).
vocab.example: La medicina está en la mesa.
vocab.exampleEn: The medicine is on the table.

vocab.example: Tengo una cita con la doctora a las diez.
vocab.exampleEn: I have an appointment with the doctor at ten.

vocab.example: Tienes que descansar y tomar mucha agua.
vocab.exampleEn: You have to rest and drink lots of water.

vocab.note: To someone you call usted: ¡Que se mejore!
Spain: el jersey.
Mexico: la chamarra; Spain and many countries: la chaqueta; Argentina: la campera.
Mexico: la playera; Spain and many countries: la camiseta.
Singular and plural both mean one pair: el pantalón / los pantalones.

vocab.exampleEn: The blue skirt is very pretty.

vocab.example: Ana lleva un vestido rojo a la fiesta.
vocab.exampleEn: Ana is wearing a red dress to the party.

vocab.note: Mexico: los tenis (shoes); el tenis is also the sport. Spain: las zapatillas (de deporte).

vocab.example: Hoy llevo pantalón negro y una chamarra.
vocab.exampleEn: Today I'm wearing black pants and a jacket.

vocab.note: Mexico City: a privately run minibus on a fixed route; also called el micro or el microbús.
vocab.example: El pesero pasa por la avenida cada diez minutos.
vocab.exampleEn: The minibus comes along the avenue every ten minutes.

vocab.note: A van that works like a small pesero; also called la vagoneta.
vocab.example: La combi va hasta el mercado.
vocab.exampleEn: The van goes as far as the market.

vocab.note: Mexico: un taxi de sitio = a taxi from a fixed stand with a base. Also "place, site" everywhere.
vocab.example: Hay un sitio de taxis enfrente del hotel.
vocab.exampleEn: There's a taxi stand opposite the hotel.

vocab.note: Feminine in Mexico: la terminal de autobuses (also la central de autobuses). Chile, Colombia, Peru and Venezuela prefer el terminal.
vocab.example: La terminal de autobuses está lejos del centro.
vocab.exampleEn: The bus station is far from downtown.

vocab.example: Espere el tren en el andén.
vocab.exampleEn: Wait for the train on the platform.

vocab.note: The word on Mexico City metro signs. People also say hacer transbordo. Its other meaning is "mail, correspondence".
vocab.example: En Pino Suárez hay correspondencia con la línea 2.
vocab.exampleEn: At Pino Suárez you can change to line 2.

vocab.note: Mexico: the named district in every address (Col. Roma Norte). Also "cologne" (perfume).
vocab.example: Vivo en la colonia Del Valle.
vocab.exampleEn: I live in the Del Valle neighbourhood.

vocab.note: Mexico: the fare you pay. In much of South America also a ticket (un pasaje de avión).

vocab.exampleEn: I'm going to the museum. Where do I get off?

meanings: Stop, please! (I'm getting off: said to a pesero driver)
vocab.note: What passengers call out to the driver of a pesero or combi. Also: ¡En la esquina, por favor!

vocab.exampleEn: I've had a cough since Monday.

vocab.example: El niño tose mucho en la noche.
vocab.exampleEn: The boy coughs a lot at night.

vocab.note: Soy alérgico a… / Soy alérgica a… = I'm allergic to …
Also el resfriado. Mexicans often just say tengo gripa.
vocab.example: No es nada grave, es un catarro.
vocab.exampleEn: It's nothing serious, it's a cold.

vocab.note: Also "recipe" in cooking. In Mexico antibiotics are sold only with a receta.
vocab.example: Para este antibiótico necesita una receta.
vocab.exampleEn: You need a prescription for this antibiotic.

vocab.example: El consultorio está junto a la farmacia.
vocab.exampleEn: The doctor's office is next to the pharmacy.

vocab.example: Tome una cucharada de jarabe cada ocho horas.
vocab.exampleEn: Take a spoonful of syrup every eight hours.

vocab.note: Masculine although it ends in -a, like el problema.
With estar: Estoy mareada.
Hospital signs: Urgencias (emergency department).

vocab.example: La ambulancia llega en diez minutos.
vocab.exampleEn: The ambulance arrives in ten minutes.

vocab.note: Me duele la garganta = I have a sore throat.
vocab.example: Me duele la garganta y tengo tos.
vocab.exampleEn: I have a sore throat and a cough.

meanings: What's wrong? (formal: what symptoms do you have?)
vocab.note: What a doctor asks a patient. To a friend: ¿Qué tienes?
vocab.exampleEn: Good morning. What seems to be the problem?

vocab.example: Ayer fui al mercado con mi mamá.
vocab.exampleEn: Yesterday I went to the market with my mom.
Last night we watched a movie.

vocab.note: Also antier in Mexico, informal.
vocab.exampleEn: My cousins arrived the day before yesterday.

vocab.note: Goes after the noun and agrees: el año pasado, la semana pasada.
vocab.exampleEn: Last week I worked a lot.

vocab.note: una vez = once; dos veces = twice; la última vez = the last time. z → c in the plural.

vocab.exampleEn: What time did the class finish?

vocab.note: Very common in Mexico; volver means the same.
vocab.example: Regresé a casa a las diez.
vocab.exampleEn: I got back home at ten.
We decided to go to the beach.

vocab.note: Irregular participle: abierto (he abierto).

forms.present: encuentro, encuentras, encuentra, encontramos, encontráis, encuentran
forms.subjunctive: encuentre, encuentres, encuentre, encontremos, encontréis, encuentren

vocab.note: o → ue in the present (encuentro); the preterite is regular: encontré, encontró.

vocab.example: Olvidé el pasaporte en el hotel.
vocab.exampleEn: I left my passport at the hotel.

forms.present: nazco, naces, nace, nacemos, nacéis, nacen
forms.subjunctive: nazca, nazcas, nazca, nazcamos, nazcáis, nazcan

vocab.note: Usually in the preterite: nací, naciste, nació. yo present nazco.
vocab.exampleEn: I was born in Monterrey in 1995.

forms.present: doy, das, da, damos, dais, dan
forms.preterite: di, diste, dio, dimos, disteis, dieron
forms.subjunctive: dé, des, dé, demos, deis, den

vocab.note: Preterite without accents: di, dio. Commands: da (tú), dé (usted).
vocab.example: Le di un regalo a mi hermana.
vocab.exampleEn: I gave my sister a present.
I bought a souvenir in Oaxaca.
The party was a lot of fun.

vocab.note: Same form for masculine and feminine; plural increíbles.
hacer una excursión = to go on a trip or outing.

vocab.note: Only pasar changes: la pasé bien, la pasamos bien. Spain: pasarlo bien.

vocab.exampleEn: We had a great time at the party.

vocab.note: Informal (tú). Formal: ¿Qué hizo usted?
vocab.exampleEn: What did you do at the weekend?

vocab.example: Fue el mejor día de mi vida.
vocab.exampleEn: It was the best day of my life.

vocab.note: ya no = not any more.

vocab.note: todavía no = not yet.

vocab.exampleEn: I haven't finished the homework yet.
Have you ever been to Peru?

vocab.example: He visto esa película muchas veces.
vocab.exampleEn: I've seen that movie many times.

forms.present: digo, dices, dice, decimos, decís, dicen

forms.subjunctive: diga, digas, diga, digamos, digáis, digan

vocab.note: Irregular participle: roto (he roto).

vocab.exampleEn: The boy has broken a plate.

forms.present: pruebo, pruebas, prueba, probamos, probáis, prueban
forms.subjunctive: pruebe, pruebes, pruebe, probemos, probéis, prueben

forms.subjunctive: cuente, cuentes, cuente, contemos, contéis, cuenten

vocab.note: en el extranjero = abroad. A foreign person: el extranjero, la extranjera.

vocab.note: todo el mundo = everybody.

vocab.note: Same form for masculine and feminine; plural picantes.
Mexico and Central America; in much of South America and the Caribbean el ají.

vocab.example: Desde aquí se ve el volcán.
vocab.exampleEn: You can see the volcano from here.

vocab.note: montar a caballo = to ride a horse.
la telenovela = TV soap opera.

vocab.exampleEn: García Márquez won the Nobel Prize in 1982.

vocab.note: las noticias = the news (on TV, online).

vocab.exampleEn: So far, everything has gone well.

vocab.note: u before a word starting with o- or ho-: siete u ocho.
vocab.exampleEn: Do you want tea or coffee?

vocab.note: No accent. Can't be left out: Creo que sí. ¿qué? (what?) is the question word.

vocab.exampleEn: When I arrived, I called my mom.

forms.preterite: creí, creíste, creyó, creímos, creísteis, creyeron

forms.preterite: marqué, marcaste, marcó, marcamos, marcasteis, marcaron

readingList.title: La ciudad (Serie de lecturas graduadas de español para extranjeros, Español 1)
readingList.author: Diana Helena Martínez Cruz
readingList.publisher: UNAM, Centro de Enseñanza para Extranjeros (CEPE)
readingList.note: Three short stories set in Mexico City's Condesa neighbourhood, written by the National University of Mexico for its own A1 students, with exercises, answers and a glossary. A free PDF from the publisher; ideal once you've finished module 3.

readingList.title: Brandon Brown quiere un perro
readingList.author: Carol Gaab
readingList.note: An almost-nine-year-old wants a dog and his mother isn't sure, told with only about 100 different words. One of the easiest real books in Spanish; try it after the first two modules.

readingList.title: El capibara con botas
readingList.author: Mira Canion
readingList.note: A capybara who can't swim has to survive away from the water, in a story set in the Amazon with notes on Ecuador's regions. Present tense and only about 55 different words.

readingList.title: Agua tóxica
readingList.author: Mira Canion
readingList.note: A short present-tense story in the Peruvian Amazon about animals, disappearing trees and a monkey who won't keep quiet. A companion to El capibara con botas, readable in either order.

readingList.title: Tumba
readingList.author: Mira Canion
readingList.note: A teenager dreads the Day of the Dead because his grandmother seems to talk with spirits, until he finds his late grandfather's sketchbook. Present tense; pairs well with honors lesson 90.

readingList.title: Pobre Ana
readingList.author: Blaine Ray
readingList.note: A long-running classic for beginners. A Californian teenager who thinks her life is hard spends time with a host family in Mexico. The book has a present-tense and a past-tense version, so you can reread it after module 6.

readingList.title: Frida Kahlo
readingList.author: Kristy Placido
readingList.level: A1–A2 (Novice Mid–Intermediate Low; a stretch at the end of A1)
readingList.note: A short, simple biography of the Mexican painter, with many cognates. Save it for after the past-tense lessons.

readingList.title: El Ekeko: un misterio boliviano
readingList.author: Katie Baker
readingList.level: A1–A2 (Novice Mid–Intermediate Low; a stretch at the end of A1)
readingList.note: A boy in La Paz finds his grandfather's boots, a box of letters and a strange gift linked to the Alasitas festival. A good next step after the course.

readingList.title: Complete Spanish (audio course)
readingList.note: A free audio course in which a teacher builds Spanish sentences step by step with a student. Stream it or download all the audio; listen alongside the grammar lessons.

readingList.title: DELE A1 exam guide and model exam
readingList.note: The official description of every part of the exam, with the scoring rules. The Instituto Cervantes also publishes a free model exam; its short notices, ads and messages are exactly the kind of text the exam uses. Save these for lesson 24.
